dulwich.advisory: Buffer overflow in the C implementation of the apply_delta function in _pack.c in Dulwich before 0.9.9 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a crafted pack file.

Dulwich before 0.18.5, when an SSH subprocess is used, allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via an ssh URL with an initial dash character in the hostname, a related issue to CVE-2017-9800, CVE-2017-12836, CVE-2017-12976, CVE-2017-1000116, and CVE-2017-1000117.

The build_index_from_tree function in index.py in Dulwich before 0.9.9 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a commit with a directory path starting with .git/, which is not properly handled when checking out a working tree.

Affected versions of the dulwich package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write due to insufficient validation of NTFS-hostile tree entry filenames in the path-element validator. The validator failed to reject filenames containing the Windows path separator, the NTFS alternate-data-stream marker, and most NTFS 8.3 short-name aliases of .git, while the core.protectNTFS configuration was silently ignored due to an incorrect option name lookup. An attacker can craft a malicious Git repository that, when cloned or checked out on Windows, plants executable files inside the .git/hooks directory to achieve Remote Code Execution.

Affected versions of the dulwich package are vulnerable to Command Injection due to unsanitised substitution of attacker-controlled file paths into shell commands. The ProcessMergeDriver class substitutes the file path from the merge tree into the merge driver command via the %P placeholder and executes it with subprocess.run using shell=True without escaping. An attacker who can cause a victim to merge an untrusted branch can inject arbitrary shell commands through crafted file paths, resulting in Remote Code Execution.

dwave-cloud-client.advisory: Dwave-cloud-client version 0.12.0 fixes a race condition issue that occurred when multiple threads attempted to resolve remote computation results simultaneously. This problem was particularly evident during binary answer downloads from a reference link. The write operation to the `answer_data` file was not thread-safe or atomic, leading to data corruption when the same answer was downloaded multiple times in parallel. This update ensures that write operations are managed properly to prevent data corruption.

Dwave-cloud-client version 0.12.0.dev0 resolves a race condition issue that occurred when binary answer downloads were initiated multiple times in parallel. Previously, the write operation to the `answer_data` file was not thread-safe or atomic, resulting in data corruption during parallel downloads of the same answer. ecdsa.advisory: A flaw was found in all python-ecdsa versions before 0.13.3, where it did not correctly verify whether signatures used DER encoding. Without this verification, a malformed signature could be accepted, making the signature malleable. Without proper verification, an attacker could use a malleable signature to create false transactions. See: CVE-2019-14859.

An error-handling flaw was found in python-ecdsa before version 0.13.3. During signature decoding, malformed DER signatures could raise unexpected exceptions (or no exceptions at all), which could lead to a denial of service. See CVE-2019-14853.

In ecdsa 0.14, deterministic signatures verify that the signature won't leak private key through very unlikely selection of `k` value (the nonce). Nonce bit size hiding was added (hardening against Minerva attack). Please note that it DOES NOT make library secure against side channel attacks (timing attacks).
https://github.com/tlsfuzzer/python-ecdsa/commit/b516f06d0e94eca6deeb3bdb82027ad2f2f55ac6

Affected versions of the python-ecdsa package are vulnerable to Denial of Service due to improper validation of DER length fields in malformed private keys. The ecdsa.der.remove_octet_string() function accepts truncated DER input when the declared length exceeds the available buffer, and this malformed data can then reach SigningKey.from_der(), which may raise an internal IndexError instead of safely rejecting the input with UnexpectedDER or ValueError.

Ecdsa does not protects against side-channel attacks. This is because Python does not provide side-channel secure primitives (with the exception of hmac.compare_digest()), making side-channel secure programming impossible. For a sophisticated attacker observing just one operation with a private key will be sufficient to completely reconstruct the private key.
https://pypi.org/project/ecdsa/#Security

The python-ecdsa library, which implements ECDSA cryptography in Python, is vulnerable to the Minerva attack (CVE-2024-23342). This vulnerability arises because scalar multiplication is not performed in constant time, affecting ECDSA signatures, key generation, and ECDH operations. ECDSA signature verification remains unaffected. The project maintainers have stated that there is no plan to release a fix for this vulnerability, citing their security policy:
"As stated in the security policy, side-channel vulnerabilities are outside the scope of the project. This is not due to a lack of interest in side-channel secure implementations but rather because the main goal of the project is to be pure Python. Implementing side-channel-free code in pure Python is impossible. Therefore, we do not plan to release a fix for this vulnerability."
NOTE: The specs we include in this advisory differ from the publicly available on other sources. That's because research by Safety CLI Cybersecurity Team confirms that there is no plan to address this vulnerability.

Affected versions of the edumfa package are vulnerable to Authentication Bypass due to incorrect InnoDB snapshot isolation allowing one-time-use token values to be reused in a race condition. On deployments using MySQL or MariaDB with innodb_snapshot_isolation disabled, the transaction isolation level does not prevent concurrent reads of the same token value before the write that marks it as consumed is committed, enabling token replay for TOTP, HOTP, and WebAuthn token types. An attacker who can race the validation transaction can reuse a captured one-time token value to authenticate multiple times before the original validation is committed.

Affected versions of the edumfa package are vulnerable to Authentication Bypass due to missing expiration enforcement on userless Passkey and WebAuthn challenges. The challenge mechanism does not attach validity or expiration information to userless authentication challenges, allowing previously issued challenges to be replayed indefinitely. An attacker who captures a valid challenge can replay it at a later time to bypass the authentication flow.

Affected versions of the edumfa package are vulnerable to Denial of Service due to improper input validation on the /validate/check endpoint when the resolver parameter is supplied with a non-existent user. The endpoint increments the fail counters of all tokens within the specified resolver when the provided username does not match any existing user, without verifying user existence first. An unauthenticated attacker with access to the /validate/check endpoint can systematically lock out legitimate users by repeatedly incrementing token fail counters across an entire resolver.

Affected versions of the EPyT-Flow package are vulnerable to Unsafe Deserialization due to insufficient validation of JSON data processed by the REST API and file loading functions. The deserialization mechanisms in the REST API endpoints and file loading routines fail to implement proper sanity checks or input validation before reconstructing objects from JSON data, allowing maliciously crafted JSON payloads to be processed without restriction. 
https://github.com/WaterFutures/EPyT-Flow/commit/3fff9151494c7dbc72073830b734f0a7e550e385

Affected versions of the epyt-flow package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data due to unsafe dynamic importing of attacker-specified types during JSON parsing. The my_load_from_json custom deserializer used by the EPyT-Flow REST API honours a JSON type field (and also affects JSON file loading), dynamically importing the attacker-provided module/class and instantiating it with attacker-controlled arguments.

Affected versions of the ESPHome package are vulnerable to Authentication Bypass due to improper length validation in the HTTP Basic Authentication implementation for ESP-IDF platform devices. The `AsyncWebServerRequest::authenticate` method in `web_server_idf` only compares bytes up to the length of the client-supplied base64-encoded authorization value rather than performing a full comparison against the correct credentials, allowing partial password matches or empty authorization headers to pass authentication checks.

ESPHome is a system to control the ESP8266/ESP32. Anyone with web_server enabled and HTTP basic auth configured on version 2021.9.1 or older is vulnerable to an issue in which `web_server` allows over-the-air (OTA) updates without checking user defined basic auth username & password. This issue is patched in version 2021.9.2. As a workaround, one may disable or remove `web_server`.

ESPHome is a system to control your ESP8266/ESP32. A security misconfiguration in the edit configuration file API in the dashboard component of ESPHome version 2023.12.9 (command line installation) allows authenticated remote attackers to read and write arbitrary files under the configuration directory rendering remote code execution possible.  This vulnerability is patched in 2024.2.1.

Affected versions of the esphome package are vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) due to unsanitized content being served with an HTML content type. The /edit endpoint in the dashboard component allows a remote authenticated user to inject arbitrary JavaScript into configuration files without sanitization, and that script is subsequently rendered with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`. An attacker who is authenticated can craft a POST to `/edit?configuration=[file]` that includes a malicious script and then have a victim visit `/edit?configuration=[file]`, enabling exfiltration of session cookies and unauthorized operations such as reading, editing, deleting configuration files and flashing firmware on managed boards.

API endpoints in dashboard component of ESPHome affected versions (command line installation) are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) allowing remote attackers to carry out attacks against a logged user of the dashboard to perform operations on configuration files (create, edit, delete). It is possible for a malicious actor to create a specifically crafted web page that triggers a cross-site request against ESPHome, this allows bypassing the authentication for API calls on the platform. This vulnerability allows bypassing authentication on API calls accessing configuration file operations on behalf of a logged user. In order to trigger the vulnerability, the victim must visit a weaponized page.

Affected versions of the esphome package are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) due to an integer overflow in a protobuf decoder bounds check. The API component’s protobuf decoder in components/api/proto.cpp performs the bounds check ptr + field_length > end, which can overflow when a malicious client supplies a very large field_length, bypassing the out-of-bounds check and triggering invalid memory reads. An attacker with network access to port 6053 can exploit this by sending a crafted plaintext API message to crash and reboot the device (no authentication required when the plaintext API protocol is used, while Noise-encrypted API sessions require knowledge of the encryption key), resulting in a sustained denial of service.

eth-abi.advisory:
Eth-abi versions above 4.2.0 are susceptible to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack when attempting to parse zero-sized types (ZST). Such parsing, despite being compliant with the ABI specifications, can result in excessive memory allocation if malicious ZST tuples are processed. A potential mitigation strategy involves prohibiting the parsing of ZST to prevent this vulnerability from being exploited.
https://github.com/ethereum/eth-abi/commit/7db682955568b01faf0858ac14bc73c624e5dd10

Ethereum ABI (Application Binary Interface) library versions before 5.0.1 are susceptible to a vulnerability due to a recursive pointer issue. This flaw can trigger an OverflowError when decoding specially crafted payloads. The vulnerability specifically arises when attempting to decode deep nested arrays encoded in hex, as demonstrated by inputs causing Python integers to exceed the size that can be converted to C ssize_t. This issue underscores the importance of carefully handling array decoding to prevent potential overflows, emphasizing the need for appropriate validation and error handling mechanisms in applications processing such data.

ethyca-fides.advisory:
Ethyca-fides 2.1.0 addresses a race condition vulnerability that occurred during the initialization of the FidesConfig class. This vulnerability could lead to unexpected behavior or incorrect security configurations if two threads attempted to modify the security attribute simultaneously. The fix ensures that the security attribute is safely initialized as an SecuritySettings object and that the test_mode attribute is correctly set using the get_test_mode() function.
https://github.com/ethyca/fides/pull/1718/commits/22df5c9917a8a3b43b40dfcb1a4c246f74e6d36c

Ethyca-fides 2.15.1 fixes a high severity path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2023-36827) present in versions prior to 2.15.1. It allowed remote attackers to access arbitrary files on the Fides webserver container's filesystem. If Fides is deployed behind a reverse proxy as recommended in Ethyca's security best practices, and the reverse proxy is an AWS application load balancer, the vulnerability cannot be exploited. Also, any secrets supplied to the container using environment variables rather than a fides.toml configuration file are unaffected by this vulnerability.
https://github.com/ethyca/fides/security/advisories/GHSA-r25m-cr6v-p9hq

Ethyca-fides 2.22.1 addresses the moderate severity vulnerability CVE-2023-46126. This issue affected versions of Fides before 2.22.1, where the privacy policy URL field in consent and privacy notices was not properly validated. Malicious users with contributor access or higher could exploit this to execute arbitrary JavaScript on integrated websites. The patch now properly sanitizes input, preventing such attacks. https://github.com/ethyca/fides/security/advisories/GHSA-fgjj-5jmr-gh83

Ethyca's Fides 2.22.1 patches a high-severity SSRF vulnerability (CVE-2023-46124) affecting versions before 2.22.1. This vulnerability allowed attackers with certain API access to make internal system requests that could lead to data breaches. The update is crucial for users with CONNECTOR_TEMPLATE_REGISTER scope and should be applied immediately to secure systems.
https://github.com/ethyca/fides/security/advisories/GHSA-jq3w-9mgf-43m4

Ethyca-fides 2.22.1 fixes a vulnerability identified as CVE-2023-46125. The issue was found with the GET api/v1/config endpoint. It allowed Admin UI users with roles lower than the owner role, such as the viewer role, to retrieve the configuration information using the API. Even though the configuration data was filtered to suppress most sensitive information, it still contained details about the internals and backend infrastructure like server addresses, ports, and database usernames. 
https://github.com/ethyca/fides/security/advisories/GHSA-rjxg-rpg3-9r89

Ethyca-fides 2.23.3 addresses the security vulnerability CVE-2023-47114. This vulnerability allowed for HTML injection that could lead to phishing attacks or malicious JavaScript execution when accessing HTML pages via the file:// protocol.
https://github.com/ethyca/fides/commit/74a095f490ea2f1db8bf18a1605ccbee8846373c.

Ethyca-fides 2.24.0 includes a fix for CVE-2023-48224: Cryptographically Weak Generation of One-Time Codes for Identity Verification.
https://github.com/ethyca/fides/security/advisories/GHSA-82vr-5769-6358

Fides is an open-source privacy engineering platform. The Fides webserver requires a connection to a hosted PostgreSQL database for persistent storage of application data. If the password used by the web server for this database connection includes special characters such as `@` and `$`, the webserver startup fails and the part of the password following the special character is exposed in web server error logs. This is caused by improper escaping of the SQLAlchemy password string. As a result, users are subject to partial exposure of hosted database passwords in web server logs.

Affected versions of the ethyca-fides package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to a masking function bug that fails to obfuscate nested sensitive fields. The `keyfile_creds.private_key` property within the `BigQuerySchema` is not masked by the internal function that applies Pydantic `sensitive` annotations, causing it to be returned in plaintext through endpoints such as `GET /api/v1/connections`, `GET /api/v1/connection/{connection_key}`, `GET /api/v1/system/{system_key}`, and related PATCH operations. An attacker who is an authenticated Admin UI user (other than those with the Approver role) or an API user authorized to call these endpoints can retrieve the BigQuery integration private key in cleartext, exposing Google Cloud secrets to unauthorized access.

Fides affected versions use the polyfill.io domain to support legacy browsers like IE11 that do not support the fetch standard. This allows users of pre-2017 browsers to potentially download and execute malicious scripts from polyfill.io when compromised. Although no exploitation has been identified, the vulnerability has been patched. On June 27, 2024, Cloudflare and Namecheap intervened to prevent polyfill.io from resolving to the compromised service, rendering this vulnerability unexploitable. Prior to this intervention, the impacts on confidentiality, integrity, and availability were high. Clients can mitigate risk by using modern browsers that support the fetch standard.

In ethyca-fides affected versions, a timing-based username enumeration vulnerability exists in the Fides Webserver authentication process. This security flaw enables an unauthenticated attacker to discern the existence of valid usernames by analyzing the server's response times to login requests. The discernible difference in response times between valid and invalid usernames can be exploited to systematically enumerate users on the system, potentially compromising user privacy and serving as a stepping stone for further attacks.

Versions ethyca-fides are vulnerable to Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security (CWE-602). The user invite acceptance API endpoint lacks server-side password policy enforcement, allowing users to set weak passwords by bypassing client-side validations. This vulnerability enables attackers to compromise accounts through brute-force or guessing attacks using easily obtainable passwords.

Affected versions of the ethyca-fides package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling due to misidentifying client IPs behind proxies and maintaining per-instance, in-memory rate-limit counters. The `fides.api.util.endpoint_utils.fides_limiter` configured a SlowAPI `Limiter` with `get_remote_address` as the key function and process-local counters, causing limits to key on the proxy/load-balancer IP and fragment across workers rather than applying to the actual client.

Affected versions of the ethyca-fides package are vulnerable to Insufficient Session Expiration due to failure to invalidate active sessions and authentication tokens after a user changes their password in the Admin UI. The `src/fides/api/api/v1/endpoints/user_endpoints.py` handlers `update_user_password` and `force_update_password` updated the password without revoking the user’s associated OAuth client or marking existing JWTs invalid, while token checks in `src/fides/api/oauth/utils.py` accepted tokens based solely on cryptographic integrity and expiry rather than the current password state.

Affected versions of the ethyca-fides package are vulnerable to Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts due to the lack of authentication-specific rate limiting on the Admin UI login flow. The `POST /api/v1/login` endpoint relies only on a coarse, system-wide IP rate limit applied across all API traffic—without dedicated authentication-scoped throttling—leaving the login route weak against automated guessing.

Affected versions of the ethyca-fides package are vulnerable to Missing Authorization due to the OAuth client creation and update endpoints allowing scope assignment without verifying that the requester already possesses those scopes. The `src/fides/api/api/v1/endpoints/oauth_endpoints.py` module’s `create_client` and `set_client_scopes` handlers validated scope names against `SCOPE_REGISTRY` but, before the fix, did not call `verify_client_can_assign_scopes` to ensure the caller’s token included those scopes, enabling arbitrary scope assignment.

The Fides webserver is vulnerable to a type of Denial of Service (DoS) attack. Attackers can exploit a weakness in the connector template upload feature to upload a malicious zip bomb file, resulting in resource exhaustion and service unavailability for all users of the Fides webserver. This vulnerability affects Fides versions `2.11.0` through `2.15.1`. Exploitation is limited to users with elevated privileges with the `CONNECTOR_TEMPLATE_REGISTER` scope, which includes root users and users with the owner role. The vulnerability has been patched in Fides version `2.16.0`. Users are advised to upgrade to this version or later to secure their systems against this threat. There is no known workaround to remediate this vulnerability without upgrading. If an attack occurs, the impact can be mitigated by manually or automatically restarting the affected container.

Fides is an open-source privacy engineering platform for managing data privacy requests and privacy regulations. The Fides webserver is vulnerable to a type of Denial of Service (DoS) attack. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability to upload zip files containing malicious SVG bombs (similar to a billion laughs attack), causing resource exhaustion in Admin UI browser tabs and creating a persistent denial of service of the 'new connector' page (`datastore-connection/new`). This vulnerability affects Fides versions `2.11.0` through `2.15.1`. Exploitation is limited to users with elevated privileges with the `CONNECTOR_TEMPLATE_REGISTER` scope, which includes root users and users with the owner role. The vulnerability has been patched in Fides version `2.16.0`. Users are advised to upgrade to this version or later to secure their systems against this threat. There is no known workaround to remediate this vulnerability without upgrading.

Ethyca-fides 2.19.0 includes a fix for CVE-2023-41319: Remote Code Execution in Custom Integration Upload.
https://github.com/ethyca/fides/security/advisories/GHSA-p6p2-qq95-vq5h

Fides affected versions are vulnerable to a security issue involving the SERVER_SIDE_FIDES_API_URL configuration environment variable used by the Fides Privacy Center. This variable typically contains a URL with a private IP address, private domain name, and/or port. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability to make an HTTP GET request from the Privacy Center, disclosing the value of this server-side URL. This disclosure could provide the attacker with information on server-side ports, private IP addresses, and/or private domain names.

In ethyca-fides affected versions, the Email Templating feature implements Jinja2 without adequate input sanitization or rendering environment restrictions. This oversight creates a vulnerability to Server-Side Template Injection, potentially allowing Remote Code Execution by privileged users. In this context, a privileged user is defined as an Admin UI user with either the default 'Owner' or 'Contributor' role. Such users can exploit this vulnerability to escalate their access and execute arbitrary code on the underlying Fides Webserver container where the Jinja template rendering function operates.

Affected versions of the ethyca-fides package are vulnerable to Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to the absence of sanitisation on client-controlled description overrides when HTML-formatted banner descriptions are enabled. The fides.js script accepts a fides_description value from a URL query parameter, a JavaScript global, or a cookie, and writes it directly into the DOM as live HTML without routing it through the server-side nh3 sanitiser that the rendering path was designed to trust. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious link containing an HTML payload in the fides_description parameter, which executes arbitrary JavaScript in the embedding site's origin when the consent banner renders, with the cookie delivery source enabling the payload to persist across all subdomains until the visitor clears their cookies.

Affected versions of the ethyca-fides package are vulnerable to Authorization Bypass due to the privacy request workflow allowing an administrator to approve duplicate requests without verifying the requester's identity. When both subject_identity_verification_required and privacy_request_duplicate_detection.enabled are set to true, a privacy request that is classified as a duplicate before its OTP identity verification completes is still presented in the administrative interface with Approve, Deny, and Delete options, so an administrator triaging duplicates can approve the request and have it processed as if verification had succeeded.

Eventlet before 0.35.2, as used in dnspython before 2.6.0, allows remote attackers to interfere with DNS name resolution by quickly sending an invalid packet from the expected IP address and source port, aka a "TuDoor" attack. In other words, dnspython does not have the preferred behavior in which the DNS name resolution algorithm would proceed, within the full time window, in order to wait for a valid packet. 
NOTE: dnspython 2.6.0 is unusable for a different reason that was addressed in 2.6.1.

Eventlet affected versions contain a vulnerability in HTTP header processing within the WSGI implementation. This flaw could allow attackers to craft specially formatted headers, potentially causing header name collisions or overwriting important headers in the WSGI environment. Such manipulation could lead to security issues depending on how applications process these headers.

Affected versions of the eventlet package are vulnerable to Request Smuggling due to improper handling of HTTP trailer sections. The eventlet.wsgi module’s _chunked_read method read only a single line after the terminating 0\r\n chunk and failed to consume remaining trailer lines, leaving bytes in the connection buffer that could be interpreted as the start of a subsequent request.

everyrow.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Command Injection. The upload handler constructs a curl command using user-controlled values without shell quoting. An attacker can exploit this by supplying crafted input containing shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying system.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure. The server includes full stack traces in error responses, and exposes poll tokens as plaintext query parameters in progress URLs where they are visible in server logs and browser history. An attacker can exploit this by triggering errors to obtain implementation details for further attacks, or by reading server logs to extract poll tokens and access task results belonging to other users.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Missing Authorization. The `everyrow_progress` and `everyrow_cancel` endpoints perform no task ownership checks, and the ownership check on the results endpoint is fail-open — silently continuing when verification fails. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a known or guessed task ID to poll, cancel, or retrieve results belonging to another authenticated user.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Replay Attack. Auth codes and refresh tokens are re-stored using non-atomic operations, allowing concurrent requests to overwrite tokens and create replay opportunities. Additionally, the OAuth state token is not consumed atomically in `handle_start`, leaving a window in which the same state token can be reused. An attacker can exploit this by replaying a captured OAuth state, auth code, or refresh token to hijack an authentication flow.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Security Misconfiguration. The `ALLOW_NO_AUTH` environment variable disables authentication for any non-empty string value rather than only the strict value `"1"`. An attacker or misconfigured deployment can exploit this by setting the variable to a value such as `"false"` or `"0"` with the intent to keep auth enabled, while the application silently disables it.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). The URL fetching implementation does not validate targets against private IP ranges, loopback addresses, cloud metadata endpoints, or re-validate hostnames at request time, and does not unwrap IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses before checking against blocked networks. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a crafted URL — including bypass variants such as `::ffff:127.0.0.1` — to make the server issue requests to internal infrastructure or cloud metadata endpoints.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Replay Attack. Download tokens are not single-use — the download endpoint does not consume the token upon a successful request. An attacker who obtains a download URL can exploit this by replaying it an arbitrary number of times to access another user's result data.

executorch.advisory: Affected versions of the ExecuTorch package are vulnerable to Heap-based Buffer Overflow due to missing bounds checks when copying tensor data during model loading. The prim_ops::et_copy_index() kernel in kernels/prim_ops/et_copy_index.cpp failed to verify that the computed destination offset plus copy length fits within the allocated size before calling memcpy, which allows writes past the end of the heap buffer.

Affected versions of the ExecuTorch package are vulnerable to Heap-based Buffer Overflow due to missing bounds validation in the prim_ops::et_copy_index routine used while loading and executing models. The et_copy_index(KernelRuntimeContext&, EValue**) implementation computes an offset = index * size_copy_from and then calls memcpy into the heap-allocated copy_to tensor without first ensuring offset + size_copy_from is within copy_to.element_size() * copy_to.numel(), enabling an out-of-bounds write when indices or tensor shapes are inconsistent.

Affected versions of the executorch package are vulnerable to Integer Overflow due to missing bounds checks when calculating buffer offsets during model loading. The HierarchicalAllocator::get_offset_address() method in runtime/core/hierarchical_allocator.h adds the offset_bytes and size_bytes values without validating for wraparound, which can yield a pointer outside the allocated buffer.

Affected versions of the executorch package are vulnerable to Integer Overflow due to missing bounds checks when computing allocation end addresses during ExecuTorch model loading. The MemoryAllocator::allocate() routine in runtime/core/memory_allocator.h calculates an end pointer from a size derived while parsing model buffers without detecting wraparound, allowing overlapping allocations to occur.

Affected versions of the ExecuTorch package are vulnerable to Heap-based Buffer Overflow due to missing bounds validation when parsing tensor metadata from untrusted model files. The parseTensor implementations in runtime/executor/tensor_parser_aten.cpp and runtime/executor/tensor_parser_portable.cpp previously did not enforce kTensorDimensionLimit on the sizes() field before using it to allocate and index heap buffers, enabling oversized ranks to trigger out-of-bounds writes.

Affected versions of the ExecuTorch package are vulnerable to Integer Overflow due to unchecked multiplication in memory allocation calculations. The allocate method in the MemoryAllocator class performs multiplication of user-controlled size values with sizeof(T) without verifying whether this operation would overflow, which can result in allocating memory regions smaller than intended. An attacker can exploit this by providing maliciously crafted ExecuTorch model files with large size values that cause integer overflow during allocation, leading to heap buffer overflows and potentially achieving arbitrary code execution.

A heap-buffer-overflow vulnerability in the loading of ExecuTorch methods can cause the runtime to crash and potentially result in code execution or other undesirable effects. This issue affects ExecuTorch prior to commit 93b1a0c15f7eda49b2bc46b5b4c49557b4e9810f

exiv2.advisory: Affected versions of the Exiv2 package are vulnerable to Denial of Service due to quadratic performance complexity in ICC profile parsing. The jpegBase::readMetadata() method contains an inefficient algorithm that exhibits quadratic time complexity when processing ICC profiles embedded in JPEG image files, causing excessive processing time on crafted inputs.

Affected versions of the Exiv2 package are vulnerable to Denial of Service due to an out-of-bounds read during metadata write operations. The Exiv2::MemIo::write method and related metadata processing functions in epsimage.cpp perform unsafe memory operations when writing metadata to crafted image files, triggering segmentation faults during the write process.
Exiv2 0.26 contains a heap buffer overflow in tiff parser.
Exiv2 0.26 contains a stack out of bounds read in JPEG2000 parser.
A stack out of bounds read vulnerability exists in Exiv2 library 0.26 within the webp parser.

Exiv2 (Python bindings to exiv2 C++ library) 0.15.0 and 0.14.1 ship with libexiv2 version 0.28.0, which is affected by CVE-2023-44398: An out-of-bounds write was found in Exiv2 version v0.28.0. The vulnerable function, 'BmffImage::brotliUncompress', is new in v0.28.0, so earlier versions of Exiv2 are _not_ affected. The out-of-bounds write is triggered when Exiv2 is used to read the metadata of a crafted image file. An attacker could potentially exploit the vulnerability to gain code execution, if they can trick the victim into running Exiv2 on a crafted image file.
https://github.com/jim-easterbrook/python-exiv2/commit/61c1365e4fcd09aaf391ad1d8435d9fab0715db7
https://github.com/Exiv2/exiv2/security/advisories/GHSA-hrw9-ggg3-3r4r

Affected versions of the Exiv2 package are vulnerable to Denial of Service due to unbounded recursion in the QuickTimeVideo::multipleEntriesDecoder function. The QuickTimeVideo::multipleEntriesDecoder method, introduced in version 0.28.0, fails to limit recursion depth when processing crafted video metadata, leading to stack exhaustion. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a specially crafted video file to Exiv2’s metadata reader, causing the Exiv2 process to crash and resulting in denial of service for local users or dependent systems.

Affected versions of the Exiv2 package are vulnerable to Denial of Service due to an out-of-bounds read in the QuickTimeVideo::NikonTagsDecoder function. The QuickTimeVideo::NikonTagsDecoder method, introduced in version 0.28.0 and present in version 0.28.1, fails to validate buffer boundaries when processing crafted video metadata, leading to unintended memory access. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a malicious video file that triggers the out-of-bounds read, causing the Exiv2 process to crash and resulting in denial of service.

A heap buffer overflow was found in Exiv2 versions v0.28.0 to v0.28.4. Versions prior to v0.28.0, such as v0.27.7, are not affected. Exiv2 is a command-line utility and C++ library for reading, writing, deleting, and modifying the metadata of image files. The heap overflow is triggered when Exiv2 is used to write metadata into a crafted image file. An attacker could potentially exploit the vulnerability to gain code execution if they can trick the victim into running Exiv2 on a crafted image file. Note that this bug is only triggered when writing the metadata, which is a less frequently used Exiv2 operation than reading the metadata. For example, to trigger the bug in the Exiv2 command-line application, you need to add an extra command-line argument such as fixiso.

Fastapi 0.30.0 avoids/fixes a potential security issue: as the returned object is passed directly to Pydantic, if the returned object was a subclass of the `response_model` (e.g. you return a `UserInDB` that inherits from `User` but contains extra fields, like `hashed_password`, and `User` is used in the `response_model`), it would still pass the validation (because `UserInDB` is a subclass of `User`) and the object would be returned as-is, including the `hashed_password`. To fix this, the declared `response_model` is cloned, if it is a Pydantic model class (or contains Pydantic model classes in it, e.g. in a `List[Item]`), the Pydantic model class(es) will be a different one (the "cloned" one). So, an object that is a subclass won't simply pass the validation and returned as-is, because it is no longer a sub-class of the cloned `response_model`. Instead, a new Pydantic model object will be created with the contents of the returned object. So, it will be a new object (made with the data from the returned one), and will be filtered by the cloned `response_model`, containing only the declared fields as normally.

Fastapi version 0.65.2 includes a security fix for CVE-2021-32677: FastAPI versions lower than 0.65.2 that used cookies for authentication in path operations that received JSON payloads sent by browsers were vulnerable to a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attack. In versions lower than 0.65.2, FastAPI would try to read the request payload as JSON even if the content-type header sent was not set to application/json or a compatible JSON media type (e.g. application/geo+json). A request with a content type of text/plain containing JSON data would be accepted and the JSON data would be extracted. Requests with content type text/plain are exempt from CORS preflights, for being considered Simple requests. The browser will execute them right away including cookies, and the text content could be a JSON string that would be parsed and accepted by the FastAPI application. The request data is now parsed as JSON only if the content-type header is application/json or another JSON compatible media type like application/geo+json. It's best to upgrade to the latest FastAPI, but if updating is not possible then a middleware or a dependency that checks the content-type header and aborts the request if it is not application/json or another JSON compatible content type can act as a mitigating workaround.

fastapi-sso.advisory: Affected versions of fastapi-sso are vulnerable to Race Condition [CWE-362]. When multiple concurrent login requests are processed simultaneously, the state shared between requests could allow one user to unintentionally obtain another user's access token and assume their identity. The vulnerability exists in the SSO login flow, where the provider instance state is not properly isolated between concurrent requests. This could be exploited in high concurrency scenarios by timing login requests precisely. The fix introduces async locking to ensure requests are processed sequentially and providers must be used within an async context manager.

Affected versions of the fastapi-sso package are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) due to improper validation of the OAuth state parameter during the authentication callback. The fastapi_sso.get_login_url method can generate a state value but does not persist it or bind it to the user’s session, and fastapi_sso.verify_and_process subsequently accepts the state provided in callback query parameters without comparing it to a trusted local value.

Affected versions of the fastapi-sso package are vulnerable to OAuth login CSRF due to missing OAuth state validation. The OAuth callback/login flow fails to verify that the returned state parameter matches the originally issued value, allowing a request to be accepted without anti-CSRF binding to the initiating session.

fastecdsa.advisory: An issue was discovered in fastecdsa before 2.1.2. When using the NIST P-256 curve in the ECDSA implementation, the point at infinity is mishandled. This means that for an extreme value in k and s^-1, the signature verification fails even if the signature is correct. This behavior is not solely a usability problem. There are some threat models where an attacker can benefit by successfully guessing users for whom signature verification will fail.

Fastecdsa 2.1.5 fixes the timing leakage from nonce bit length. This is also known as the 'Minerva' vulnerability. See: <https://minerva.crocs.fi.muni.cz/>.
https://github.com/indutny/elliptic/commit/ec735edde187a43693197f6fa3667ceade751a3a

Versions of the package fastecdsa before 2.3.2 are vulnerable to Use of Uninitialized Variable on the stack, via the curvemath_mul function in src/curveMath.c, due to being used and interpreted as user-defined type. Depending on the variable's actual value it could be arbitrary free(), arbitrary realloc(), null pointer dereference and other. Since the stack can be controlled by the attacker, the vulnerability could be used to corrupt allocator structure, leading to possible heap exploitation. The attacker could cause denial of service by exploiting this vulnerability. See CVE-2024-21502.

fastfeedparser.advisory: Affected versions of the fastfeedparser package are vulnerable to Denial of Service via Uncontrolled Recursion due to the parse() function following HTML meta-refresh redirects without any depth limit, visited-URL deduplication, or redirect count cap. When parse() encounters an HTML page with a meta http-equiv="refresh" tag, it recursively calls itself with the redirect URL unconditionally, allowing an attacker-controlled server to return an infinite chain of meta-refresh responses that exhausts the Python call stack. An attacker can supply a malicious feed URL that holds a server worker thread indefinitely and ultimately crashes the process via RecursionError, and can additionally chain the redirect loop to pivot SSRF requests to internal network targets.

fastmcp.advisory: Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to Improper Authentication due to a Confused Deputy flaw in the built-in OAuth authorisation flow. The /authorize endpoint—when FastMCP serves as both the OAuth Protected Resource and the Authorization Server via /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server—does not bind the dynamic client and redirect_uri to the user’s prior Entra ID consent state, allowing an attacker-controlled client to receive an authorisation code issued for the victim.

Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to unsanitized user-controlled content being embedded in the OAuth client’s callback HTML. The create_callback_html function in src/fastmcp/client/oauth_callback.py inserts the message parameter—including values propagated from query parameters such as error—directly into the page without HTML escaping, enabling reflected XSS.

Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to Command Injection due to improper neutralization of the server_name value when constructing and launching a Windows deep link during the Cursor installer flow. The generate_cursor_deeplink(server_name, …) function embeds server_name directly into a cursor://… query string, which is then executed by open_deeplink() with shell=True on Windows (invoking cmd.exe /c start), allowing command metacharacters such as & or | in server_name to escape the intended command.

Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to incorrect handling of the OAuth resource parameter during token issuance. In src/fastmcp/server/auth/oauth_proxy.py, the OAuthProxy initialises JWTIssuer with issuer=str(self.base_url) and audience=f"{str(self.base_url).rstrip('/')}/mcp", so issued access and refresh tokens are bound to the proxy base_url rather than the client-supplied target resource, preventing MCP servers from verifying that a token was issued specifically for them.

Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to missing consent verification in the OAuth proxy callback flow. Specifically, OAuthProxy._handle_idp_callback accepts a valid state and IdP code pair and forwards the browser to the client callback without verifying that the same browser session actually completed the consent step, which makes OAuth integrations vulnerable when the identity provider can skip consent for previously authorized clients.

Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to Command Injection due to improper neutralization of shell metacharacters in server names. The fastmcp install claude-code and fastmcp install gemini-cli installation paths pass a server name into subprocess.run(), and on Windows the target CLI may resolve to a .cmd wrapper executed through cmd.exe, which interprets metacharacters such as & in the flattened command string.

Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and Path Traversal due to improper path parameter handling in URL construction. Specifically, fastmcp/utilities/openapi/director.py implements RequestDirector._build_url() by directly substituting untrusted path parameter values into path_template without URL-encoding, then passing the result to urllib.parse.urljoin(), which normalizes dot-dot-slash traversal sequences and allows the final request path to escape the intended API prefix.

Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to an Improper Input Validation bypass of storage size limits, due to the FileUpload provider trusting client-declared metadata rather than measuring the actual payload. The store_files tool in src/fastmcp/apps/file_upload.py compared max_file_size against the untrusted size field supplied by the caller in each file object, rather than the length of the base64-encoded data field, allowing the declared and actual sizes to diverge arbitrarily.

Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to a Confused Deputy / credential leakage issue due to HTTP transports unconditionally forwarding the inbound request's Authorization header to any remote server a Client connects to. StreamableHttpTransport and SSETransport in the client transport layer called get_http_headers(include={"authorization"}) during connect_session on every instantiation, a behavior designed for the proxy pattern but which fired for any fastmcp.Client(...) opened inside a server-side tool handler, since tool handlers execute within the inbound server request context. When a FastMCP server with bearer-token authentication exposes a tool that calls out to a third-party MCP server, the inbound caller's bearer token is transmitted verbatim to that third party, exposing it to the third party's operator, logs, and downstream systems and enabling credential replay against the original FastMCP server if the token is not audience-bound or is long-lived.

Affected versions of the fastmcp package are vulnerable to an OAuth Audience Confusion / token-reuse issue due to AuthKitProvider configuring JWTVerifier.audience from the client_id parameter rather than the server's canonical resource URL. The provider's audience check validated tokens against a tenant-wide client_id identifier instead of the per-server resource URL advertised in .well-known/oauth-protected-resource, leaving MCP servers in the same WorkOS AuthKit tenant with indistinguishable token audiences and failing to implement the audience binding prescribed by RFC 8707 Resource Indicators.

fickling.advisory: Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data due to an incomplete unsafe-imports blocklist that does not treat Python’s cProfile module as dangerous. The issue is in fickling/analysis.py where the UnsafeImports analysis used by fickling.analysis.check_safety omits cProfile, cProfile.run, and cProfile.runctx, so a pickle that calls cProfile.run() via __reduce__ is misclassified as Severity.SUSPICIOUS instead of Severity.OVERTLY_MALICIOUS.

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to an incomplete blocklist of unsafe Python modules and functions. The fickling/analysis.py UnsafeImports logic does not include runpy (including runpy.run_path() and runpy.run_module()), causing malicious pickle payloads that invoke these APIs (for example via __reduce__) to be classified as SUSPICIOUS instead of OVERTLY_MALICIOUS.

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to an incomplete denylist of unsafe imports during pickle analysis. The fickling unsafe-import detection allows GLOBAL pydoc locate. It does not explicitly block ctypes, so a crafted pickle can call pydoc.locate('ctypes.windll.kernel32.WinExec') and then invoke the returned function while still being reported as LIKELY_SAFE.

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Security Bypass due to an incomplete blocklist of unsafe Python modules in its static analyser. The unsafe_imports() method in fickling/fickle.py flags only a hardcoded tuple of module names and fails to treat imports of ctypes, importlib, runpy, code, and multiprocessing as unsafe, with ctypes also evading the NonStandardImports check because it is part of the standard library.

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Protection Mechanism Failure due to builtins imports being omitted when converting pickle bytecode into an AST. In fickling/fickle.py, Import.run() skips emitting ast.ImportFrom nodes when module is ("__builtin__", "__builtins__", "builtins"), so the UNSAFE_MODULES checks in fickling/analysis.py never see those dangerous imports during analysis.

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Security Feature Bypass due to a missing AST persistence step when interpreting the pickle OBJ-family opcodes. Specifically, Obj.run() in fickle.py pushes an ast.Call for OBJ onto the interpreter stack without recording it via interpreter.new_variable(), so when the value is later discarded with POP the call disappears from the final AST and becomes invisible to the safety analyses used by is_likely_safe(), fickling.analysis.check_safety(), and the --check-safety CLI (with the same pattern also present in NewObj.run() and NewObjEx.run()).

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to an incomplete and overly permissive trust model that treats all Python standard library imports as likely safe and suppresses analysis when a REDUCE opcode is followed by a BUILD opcode. The issue occurs in the safety interfaces is_likely_safe(), fickling.analysis.check_safety(), CLI --check-safety, always_check_safety(), and the check_safety() context manager because likely_safe_imports over-includes stdlib symbols, OvertlyBadEvals skips calls whose function name is in likely_safe_imports, and BUILD-generated __setstate__ calls are excluded from non_setstate_calls, preventing both call-level and unused-variable detection.

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data due to incomplete hooking of pickle deserialization entry points. The fickling.always_check_safety() mechanism patches pickle.load, pickle.Unpickler, and _pickle.Unpickler, but leaves pickle.loads, _pickle.load, and _pickle.loads unprotected, allowing unsafe pickle payloads to bypass the intended safety checks and execute without raising UnsafeFileError.

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to an incomplete blocklist of unsafe standard library modules. The UNSAFE_IMPORTS checks in fickling.analysis do not include uuid, _osx_support, or _aix_support, allowing pickle payloads that call uuid._get_command_stdout, _osx_support._read_output or _find_build_tool, and _aix_support._read_cmd_output to bypass UnsafeImports, NonStandardImports, and related safety checks and be classified as safe.

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data due to an incomplete block list of unsafe module imports. Specifically, fickling’s pickle analysis can incorrectly classify a crafted pickle that uses STACK_GLOBAL to resolve pty.spawn and then calls it via REDUCE as LIKELY_SAFE, because the pty module was not treated as an unsafe import and the added BUILD opcode can make the leftover stack value appear “used” to the unused-variable heuristic.

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to an incomplete block list of disallowed module imports. The fickling.analysis.check_safety() workflow fails to flag pickle payloads that reference marshal.loads and types.FunctionType, allowing fickling.fickle.Pickled.non_standard_imports() analysis to incorrectly classify a malicious pickle as “LIKELY_SAFE.”

Affected versions of the fickling package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to an incomplete unsafe-import blocklist and a logic flaw in variable-usage analysis that allows dangerous constructor calls to be treated as safe. The check_safety() API and --check-safety CLI rely on UNSAFE_IMPORTS / UnsafeImportsML.UNSAFE_MODULES plus the UnusedVariables heuristic driven by unused_assignments() in fickling/fickle.py, but omissions for stdlib network modules (for example smtplib.SMTP, imaplib.IMAP4, ftplib.FTP, poplib.POP3, telnetlib.Telnet, and nntplib.NNTP) combined with an early break that skips scanning result = <expr> enable a REDUCE + EMPTY_DICT + BUILD opcode sequence to suppress warnings and yield LIKELY_SAFE

fidesops.advisory: The Fides webserver is vulnerable to a type of Denial of Service (DoS) attack. Attackers can exploit a weakness in the connector template upload feature to upload a malicious zip bomb file, resulting in resource exhaustion and service unavailability for all users of the Fides webserver. This vulnerability affects Fides versions `2.11.0` through `2.15.1`. Exploitation is limited to users with elevated privileges with the `CONNECTOR_TEMPLATE_REGISTER` scope, which includes root users and users with the owner role. The vulnerability has been patched in Fides version `2.16.0`. Users are advised to upgrade to this version or later to secure their systems against this threat. There is no known workaround to remediate this vulnerability without upgrading. If an attack occurs, the impact can be mitigated by manually or automatically restarting the affected container.

Fides is an open-source privacy engineering platform for managing data privacy requests and privacy regulations. The Fides webserver is vulnerable to a type of Denial of Service (DoS) attack. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability to upload zip files containing malicious SVG bombs (similar to a billion laughs attack), causing resource exhaustion in Admin UI browser tabs and creating a persistent denial of service of the 'new connector' page (`datastore-connection/new`). This vulnerability affects Fides versions `2.11.0` through `2.15.1`. Exploitation is limited to users with elevated privileges with the `CONNECTOR_TEMPLATE_REGISTER` scope, which includes root users and users with the owner role. The vulnerability has been patched in Fides version `2.16.0`. Users are advised to upgrade to this version or later to secure their systems against this threat. There is no known workaround to remediate this vulnerability without upgrading.

fief-server.advisory: Fief-server 0.25.3 includes a fix for a Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) vulnerability. This could be exploited by an attacker, who could take advantage of this issue to implement code on the base system by modifying values in the embedded template. Achieving this can lead to the attacker operating commands with permissions under the manipulated process or utilizing Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) for executing code within the user's browser.

filelock.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to a TOCTOU (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) symlink vulnerability due to improper handling of symlinks during lock file creation. The vulnerability exists because the package does not adequately check for symlink manipulation between the time the lock file path is checked and the time it is used. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by creating a malicious symlink, potentially leading to unauthorized access or modification of files, which could compromise the integrity and security of the system.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Time-of-Check Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) Race Condition. The file locking mechanism in SoftFileLock._acquire() performs permission validation before file creation without using the O_NOFOLLOW flag, leading to a race window where attackers with local access can create symlinks that redirect lock operations to arbitrary files. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by creating a malicious symlink during the brief window between permission check and file creation, causing the lock to operate on unintended target files and potentially enabling unauthorized access or file corruption.

Affected versions of the filelock package are vulnerable to a Time-of-Check Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) Race Condition due to a race window between a write-permission check and lock file creation that does not prevent symlink substitution. The flaw is in filelock.SoftFileLock in src/filelock/_soft.py, where _acquire() calls raise_on_not_writable_file() and then performs os.open() on the lock path, allowing the filesystem state to change between the check and the use.

fin-infra.advisory: Affected versions of the fin-infra package are vulnerable to the use of a weak cryptographic algorithm due to using MD5 for cache keys. The cache key generation logic relies on MD5 (explicitly referenced by the Bandit suppression for B324), which can allow practical hash collisions when an attacker can influence inputs used to derive cache keys.

https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1051025

Fincity-django-allauth before 0.28.0 contained a vulnerability allowing an attacker to alter the provider specific settings for 'SCOPE' and/or 'AUTH_PARAMS' (part of the larger 'SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS' setting). The changes would persist across subsequent requests for all users, provided these settings were explicitly set within your project. These settings translate directly into request parameters, giving the attacker undesirable control over the OAuth(2) handshake. You are not affected if you did not explicitly configure these settings.

flair.advisory: Affected versions of flairNLP are vulnerable to Remote Code Execution (CWE-94) through Code Injection. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by manipulating model files loaded by ClusteringModel in flair/models/clustering.py. An attacker can craft malicious model files that, when loaded by the target application, execute arbitrary code. While exploitability requires specific conditions and is considered difficult, working exploits are publicly available. To remediate, upgrade beyond version 0.14.0 or implement strict model file validation.

flamehaven-filesearch.advisory: Affected versions of the flamehaven-filesearch package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to insufficient validation and sanitization of user-controlled filenames in the file upload endpoints. The FastAPI-based upload handlers in flamehaven_filesearch.api previously wrote uploaded content to disk using the raw client-supplied filename as part of the filesystem path, so directory traversal sequences and hidden-file names (such as .env) could escape the intended uploads directory instead of being normalized with os.path.basename().

flash-attn.advisory: Affected versions of the flash_attn package are vulnerable to Insecure Deserialisation due to the use of torch.load() without the weights_only=True parameter in the checkpoint loading mechanism. The load_checkpoint() function in checkpoint.py and the checkpoint loading code in eval.py unconditionally deserialise arbitrary Python objects via the pickle module when loading model checkpoints. An attacker can supply a crafted checkpoint file that executes arbitrary code on the victim’s system during model warmstarting or evaluation.

Flask 2.2.5 and 2.3.2 include a fix for CVE-2023-30861: When all of the following conditions are met, a response containing data intended for one client may be cached and subsequently sent by the proxy to other clients. If the proxy also caches 'Set-Cookie' headers, it may send one client's 'session' cookie to other clients. The severity depends on the application's use of the session and the proxy's behavior regarding cookies. The risk depends on all these conditions being met:
1. The application must be hosted behind a caching proxy that does not strip cookies or ignore responses with cookies.
2. The application sets 'session.permanent = True'
3. The application does not access or modify the session at any point during a request.
4. 'SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST' enabled (the default).
5. The application does not set a 'Cache-Control' header to indicate that a page is private or should not be cached.
This happens because vulnerable versions of Flask only set the 'Vary: Cookie' header when the session is accessed or modified, not when it is refreshed (re-sent to update the expiration) without being accessed or modified.
https://github.com/pallets/flask/security/advisories/GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq

Affected versions of the Flask package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to missing cache-variation headers when the session object is accessed via certain code paths. In Flask’s session handling, accessing flask.session is intended to set a Vary: Cookie response header, but session key-only access patterns (such as using the Python in operator to test for a key without reading or mutating session values) can bypass the logic that adds the header.

Affected versions of Flask (≤ 3.1.0) are vulnerable to incorrect fallback key configuration in session signing, leading to stale key usage instead of the intended current key. This flaw undermines session integrity, enabling remote attackers to forge or tamper with cookies via manipulated SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS parameters. The vulnerability exists in the itsdangerous-based signing routines within flask.sessions (fallback key list ordering).

** DISPUTED ** Flask-AppBuilder is an application development framework, built on top of Flask. When Flask-AppBuilder is set to AUTH_TYPE AUTH_OID, it allows an attacker to forge an HTTP request, that could deceive the backend into using any requested OpenID service. This vulnerability could grant an attacker unauthorised privilege access if a custom OpenID service is deployed by the attacker and accessible by the backend. This vulnerability is only exploitable when the application is using the OpenID 2.0 authorization protocol. Upgrade to Flask-AppBuilder 4.3.11 to fix the vulnerability.

Flask-AppBuilder 4.3.2 includes a fix for an Information Disclosure vulnerability.
https://github.com/dpgaspar/Flask-AppBuilder/security/advisories/GHSA-jhpr-j7cq-3jp3
Flask-appbuilder's update from dnspython 2.4.2 to 2.6.1 addresses CVE-2023-29483.

In flask-appbuilder affected versions, the authentication database login form's default cache directives allow browsers to locally store sensitive data. This poses a security risk, particularly in environments where computer resources are shared. The latest release contains a patch addressing this issue. If upgrading is not feasible, users can mitigate the vulnerability by configuring their web server to send specific HTTP headers for the /login endpoint, following the instructions provided in the GitHub Security Advisory.

User enumeration in database authentication in Flask-AppBuilder <= 4.5.3 and werkzeug >= 3.0.0. Allows for a non-authenticated user to enumerate existing usernames by timing the response time from the server when brute forcing requests to login.

Affected versions of the `Flask-AppBuilder` package are vulnerable to Open Redirect due to improper validation of the Host header in HTTP requests. The `redirect` function fails to verify that the Host header matches a trusted domain, allowing arbitrary redirection. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a request with a manipulated Host header, redirecting users to a malicious site without their knowledge or consent.

Affected versions of the flask-appbuilder package are vulnerable to Improper Authentication due to the password-reset endpoint remaining registered and reachable when non-AUTH_DB authentication (e.g., OAuth or LDAP) is enabled. The framework continued to expose password-reset routes (such as ResetMyPasswordView) even though the link was hidden in the UI, allowing local password/JWT flows to proceed without checking the external identity provider’s disabled state. An attacker with an enabled account in Flask-AppBuilder can directly invoke the reset-my-password URL while the deployment uses OAuth/LDAP and set a new password to mint JWT tokens, effectively retaining access even if they were disabled on the external provider.

Affected versions of the `Flask-AppBuilder` package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to observable response time discrepancies during authentication. The login mechanism in `Flask-AppBuilder` allows unauthenticated users to infer the existence of user accounts by measuring the time taken to respond to login attempts with valid versus invalid usernames. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple login attempts and analyzing the response times to enumerate valid usernames in the system.

Affected versions of the `Flask-AppBuilder` package are vulnerable to Open Redirect due to improper validation of redirect URLs in the OAuth implementation. The `next` parameter in the OAuth login flow is not adequately validated to ensure it points to a trusted domain, allowing manipulation by attackers. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a URL with a malicious `next` parameter, leading users to an attacker-controlled site after authentication.

Flask-AppBuilder is an application development framework, built on top of Flask. A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability has been discovered on the OAuth login page. An attacker could trick a user to follow a specially crafted URL to the OAuth login page. This URL could inject and execute malicious javascript code that would get executed on the user's browser. Affected versions of the flask-cors package are vulnerable to Improper Output Neutralization for Logs due to unsanitized request path values being written to the debug logger. In flask_cors.extension.CORS, request.path is logged via LOG.debug without normalizing or escaping CRLF characters when DEBUG logging is enabled, as evidenced by the logging site in extension.py and the fix that cleans request.path before logging.

A vulnerability in corydolphin/flask-cors version 4.0.1 allows the `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network` CORS header to be set to true by default. This behavior can expose private network resources to unauthorized external access, leading to significant security risks such as data breaches, unauthorized access to sensitive information, and potential network intrusions.

Affected versions of the flask-cors package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to flawed regex pattern prioritization in path matching logic. The package incorrectly prioritizes longer regex patterns over more specific ones when determining CORS policies for endpoints, causing less restrictive CORS configurations to be applied to sensitive paths that should have stricter access controls. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by making cross-origin requests to sensitive endpoints that inadvertently match broader regex patterns, bypassing intended CORS restrictions and potentially accessing confidential data or executing unauthorized actions from untrusted origins.

Affected versions of the flask-cors package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to inconsistent URL path handling when processing the '+' character. The package incorrectly uses the unquote_plus function on request.path, which converts '+' characters to spaces, resulting in path normalization errors that prevent proper CORS policy matching for endpoints containing '+' symbols. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by accessing endpoints with '+' characters in their paths to bypass intended CORS restrictions or cause legitimate cross-origin requests to be incorrectly blocked, potentially exposing sensitive data to unauthorized origins or disrupting application functionality.

Affected versions of the flask‑cors package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity due to case‑insensitive request path matching caused by using the try_match function, originally intended for hostnames. The cors_after_request logic applies unquote_plus to request.path and then uses try_match_pattern with caseSensitive=True only in patched versions, whereas the vulnerable behaviour uses try_match (case‑insensitive), resulting in mismatches between the intended case‑sensitive URL paths and the CORS matching. An attacker can exploit this by crafting requests with differently cased path segments that bypass restrictions on sensitive endpoints, enabling unauthorized cross‑origin access and potential data exposure.

This vulnerability occurs because Flask-Security does not fully check whether a redirect URL is relative or absolute, and modern browsers can 'fill in the blanks' for slightly malformed URLs. flask-security-too.advisory:
Flask-security-too 4.1.0 includes a fix for CVE-2021-32618: Flask-Security-Too allows redirects after many successful views (e.g. /login) by honoring the ?next query param. There is code in FS to validate that the url specified in the next parameter is either relative OR has the same netloc (network location) as the requesting URL. This check utilizes Pythons urlsplit library. However many browsers are very lenient on the kind of URL they accept and 'fill in the blanks' when presented with a possibly incomplete URL. As a concrete example - setting http://login?next=\\\github.com will pass FS's relative URL check however many browsers will gladly convert this to http://github.com. Thus an attacker could send such a link to an unwitting user, using a legitimate site and have it redirect to whatever site they want. This is considered a low severity due to the fact that if Werkzeug is used (which is very common with Flask applications) as the WSGI layer, it by default ALWAYS ensures that the Location header is absolute - thus making this attack vector mute. It is possible for application writers to modify this default behavior by setting the 'autocorrect_location_header=False'.
https://github.com/Flask-Middleware/flask-security/commit/e39bb04615050448c1b8ba4caa7dacc0edd3e405

An open redirect vulnerability in the python package Flask-Security-Too <=5.3.2 allows attackers to redirect unsuspecting users to malicious sites via a crafted URL by abusing the ?next parameter on the /login and /register routes.
https://github.com/brandon-t-elliott/CVE-2023-49438

Flask-security-too 3.4.5 includes a security fix: When a user is setting up two-factor authentication using an authenticator app, a QRcode is generated and made available via a GET request to /tf-qrcode. Since GETs do not have any CSRF protection, it is possible a malicious 3rd party could access the QRcode and therefore gain access to two-factor authentication codes. Note that the /tf-qrcode endpoint is ONLY accessible while the user is initially setting up their device. Once setup is complete, there is no vulnerability. As a workaround, you can provide your own URL for fetching the QRcode by defining SECURITY_TWO_FACTOR_QRCODE_URL and providing your own implementation (that presumably required a POST with CSRF protection). This would require changing the two-factor setup template as well.

The Python "Flask-Security-Too" package is used for adding security features to your Flask application. It is an is a independently maintained version of Flask-Security based on the 3.0.0 version of Flask-Security. In Flask-Security-Too from version 3.3.0 and before version 3.4.5, the /login and /change endpoints can return the authenticated user's authentication token in response to a GET request. Since GET requests aren't protected with a CSRF token, this could lead to a malicious 3rd party site acquiring the authentication token. Version 3.4.5 and version 4.0.0 are patched. As a workaround, if you aren't using authentication tokens - you can set the SECURITY_TOKEN_MAX_AGE to "0" (seconds) which should make the token unusable. See CVE-2021-21241.

Affected versions of the flask-security-too package are vulnerable to Improper Authentication due to the OAuth reauthentication callback marking a session as fresh after verifying an OAuth identity that does not match the current session user. In flask_security/oauth_glue.py, the oauth_verify_response() handler accepts any user resolved by _oauth_response_common() from the OAuth provider response and updates the session fs_paa freshness timestamp without confirming that the resolved identity equals the authenticated session user. An attacker operating a stale victim session can complete OAuth verification with their own provider account to satisfy the freshness requirement and then invoke freshness-protected actions such as /change-username against the victim account.

foundry-sandbox.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Command Injection. The `fetch_bare_branch` function does not validate branch names before constructing `refs/heads/` paths, allowing ref injection and path traversal. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying a crafted branch name containing path traversal sequences or malicious ref patterns to access arbitrary git refs or paths outside the intended scope.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure. Credentials embedded in git clone URLs are not properly detected and sanitized. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by accessing logs or error messages containing clone URLs to obtain sensitive credentials.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Path Traversal. The symlink boundary checks do not properly prevent traversal outside intended directories. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by creating symlinks that point outside the allowed directory boundaries to access unauthorized files.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Authentication Bypass. The identity verification mechanism can be circumvented. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by bypassing identity checks to perform unauthorized actions.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Command Injection. The git diff argument parsing does not properly validate argument order. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by manipulating the order of arguments to bypass security controls and inject malicious git commands.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). The IP address validation does not block IPv6 literal addresses. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by using IPv6 IP literals to bypass SSRF protections and access internal network resources.

Affected versions of the fpdf2 package are vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) due to an inefficient regular expression in the SVG transform parser that can trigger catastrophic backtracking. The convert_transforms() function in fpdf/svg.py uses the TRANSFORM_GETTER pattern to parse transform attributes, and the earlier pattern employed nested quantifiers that lead the Python regex engine to super-linear matching behaviour on crafted input.

fraiseql.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to SQL Injection and Authorization Bypass. The GraphQL schema fails to validate context parameters and prevent client control of authentication parameters before PostgreSQL function calls, leading to SQL injection attacks and unauthorized access through manipulation of auth-related parameters in GraphQL queries.

Affected versions of the fraiseql package are vulnerable to information disclosure due to APQ response cache keys omitting GraphQL variables. In the APQ response caching logic (e.g., src/fraiseql/middleware/apq_caching.py), cache keys were computed using only the persisted query hash instead of incorporating normalized variables, and this is addressed by introducing compute_response_cache_key().

fraiseql-confiture.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Command Injection. The `SshTunnelConfig` fields `host` and `user`, and the git reference parameters in `GitRepository.get_file_at_ref()` and `get_changed_files()`, are not validated before being passed to subprocess calls. An attacker can exploit this by supplying values containing shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying system.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Path Traversal. The `_resolve_config()` function in `cli/helpers.py` does not validate the environment name supplied via the `--env` flag before using it to construct a file path of the form `db/environments/{name}.yaml`. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a value containing path traversal sequences or absolute path components to read files outside the intended configuration directory.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to SQL Injection. The `ProductionSyncer` and `Migrator` classes construct SQL statements using f-string interpolation for table and column identifiers, and `RestoreOptions` constructs PostgreSQL connection strings by interpolating `host`, `port`, `dbname`, and `username` values directly into an f-string. An attacker can exploit this by supplying crafted identifiers or connection parameter values to manipulate executed SQL statements or inject additional connection string directives.
