In ERPNext, versions v11.0.0-beta through v13.0.2 are vulnerable to Missing Authorization, in the chat rooms functionality. A low privileged attacker can send a direct message or a group message to any member or group, impersonating themselves as the administrator. The attacker can also read chat messages of groups that they do not belong to, and of other users.

frappe.advisory: An issue was discovered in Frappe Framework 10, 11 before 11.1.46, and 12. There exists an XSS vulnerability.
An issue was discovered in Frappe Framework 10 through 12 before 12.0.4. There exists an authenticated SQL injection.
An issue was discovered in Frappe Framework 10 through 12 before 12.0.4. A server side template injection (SSTI) issue exists.

https://github.com/frappe/frappe/security/advisories/GHSA-j2w9-8xrr-7g98

Frappe is a full-stack web application framework that uses Python and MariaDB on the server side and a tightly integrated client side library. Prior to versions 14.59.0 and 15.5.0, portal pages are susceptible to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) which can be used to inject malicious JS code if user clicks on a malicious link. This vulnerability has been patched in versions 14.59.0 and 15.5.0. No known workarounds are available. See CVE-2024-24812.

Affected versions of the frappe package are vulnerable to SQL Injection due to improper input validation in database query construction. The framework fails to properly sanitize user-supplied input before incorporating it into SQL queries, allowing malicious SQL statements to be executed against the database.

Affected versions of the frappe package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to improper access control validation on sensitive endpoints. The framework fails to properly restrict access to certain API endpoints or routes that expose user account information when processing crafted requests.

Affected versions of the frappe package are vulnerable to Remote Code Execution due to improper validation of document creation parameters. The framework fails to properly validate and sanitize input when system users create certain documents through specific methods, allowing arbitrary code to be embedded and executed.

Affected versions of the frappe package are vulnerable to SQL Injection due to improper validation of user input in database queries. The framework fails to adequately sanitize specially crafted request parameters before incorporating them into SQL statements, allowing malicious SQL code to be injected and executed.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in specified versions of Frappe, used by ERPNext, specifically within the frappe.share.get_users function. This vulnerability allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary SQL commands through manipulation of the 'fields' parameter.

This is a placeholder package for the original Frappe Framework where a vulnerability was found. The vulnerability affects versions up to 14.14.3 and allows an external attacker to remotely obtain arbitrary local files. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. 
https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rfgc-5r25-fw46
https://github.com/frappe/frappe/commit/bfab7191543961c6cb77fe267063877c31b616ce

Frappe is a low code web framework written in Python and Javascript. A SQL Injection vulnerability has been identified in the Frappe Framework which could allow a malicious actor to access sensitive information. This issue has been addressed in versions 13.46.1 and 14.20.0. Users are advised to upgrade. There's no workaround to fix this without upgrading.

In core/doctype/prepared_report/prepared_report.py in Frappe 11 and 12, data files generated with Prepared Report were being stored as public files (no authentication is required to access; having a link is sufficient) instead of private files.

freeipa.advisory: The default configuration of Red Hat Enterprise IPA 1.0.0 and FreeIPA before 1.1.1 places ldap:///anyone on the read ACL for the krbMKey attribute, which allows remote attackers to obtain the Kerberos master key via an anonymous LDAP query.
Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Web UI in FreeIPA 4.x before 4.1.2 allows remote attackers to inject arbitrary web script or HTML via vectors related to breadcrumb navigation.
ipa-kra-install in FreeIPA before 4.2.2 puts the CA agent certificate and private key in /etc/httpd/alias/kra-agent.pem, which is world readable.

The cert_revoke command in FreeIPA does not check for the "revoke certificate" permission, which allows remote authenticated users to revoke arbitrary certificates by leveraging the "retrieve certificate" permission.

A vulnerability was found in ipa before 4.4. IdM's ca-del, ca-disable, and ca-enable commands did not properly check the user's permissions while modifying CAs in Dogtag. An authenticated, unauthorized attacker could use this flaw to delete, disable, or enable CAs causing various denial of service problems with certificate issuance, OCSP signing, and deletion of secret keys.

Ipa versions 4.2.x, 4.3.x before 4.3.3 and 4.4.x before 4.4.3 did not properly check the user's permissions while modifying certificate profiles in IdM's certprofile-mod command. An authenticated, unprivileged attacker could use this flaw to modify profiles to issue certificates with arbitrary naming or key usage information and subsequently use such certificates for other attacks.

Freeipa 4.6.7, 4.7.4 and 4.8.3 include a fix for CVE-2019-14867: A flaw was found in IPA in the way the internal function ber_scanf() was used in some components of the IPA server, which parsed kerberos key data. An unauthenticated attacker who could trigger parsing of the krb principal key could cause the IPA server to crash or in some conditions, cause arbitrary code to be executed on the server hosting the IPA server.
https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=CVE-2019-14867
ipa 3.0 does not properly check server identity before sending credential containing cookies

The get_user_grouplist function in the extdom plug-in in FreeIPA before 4.1.4 does not properly reallocate memory when processing user accounts, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a group list request for a user that belongs to a large number of groups.
FreeIPA 4.4.0 allows remote attackers to request an arbitrary SAN name for services.
FreeIPA might display user data improperly via vectors involving non-printable characters.

FreeIPA uses a default password policy that locks an account after 5 unsuccessful authentication attempts, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service by locking out the account in which system services run on.

FreeIPA versions 1.3.0b0 to 4.8.0rc1, which employ Samba to integrate with Microsoft's Active Directory, were discovered to be susceptible to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack known as SMBLoris. This vulnerability was detected in August 2017.

The software FreeIPA shows public visibility of DNS records from versions alpha-1-9-0 to rc_1-2-1-90 to anyone who can access the LDAP server. This exposure, related to System Network Configuration Discovery, could potentially assist an attacker in lateral movement.

FreeIPA 4.0.x before 4.0.5 and 4.1.x before 4.1.1, when 2FA is enabled, allows remote attackers to bypass the password requirement of the two-factor authentication leveraging an enabled OTP token, which triggers an anonymous bind.

A flaw was found in all ipa versions 4.x.x through 4.8.0. When sending a very long password (>= 1,000,000 characters) to the server, the password hashing process could exhaust memory and CPU leading to a denial of service and the website becoming unresponsive. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to system availability.

It was found that FreeIPA 4.2.0 and later could disclose password hashes to users having the 'System: Read Stage Users' permission. A remote, authenticated attacker could potentially use this flaw to disclose the password hashes belonging to Stage Users. This security issue does not result in disclosure of password hashes belonging to active standard users. NOTE: some developers feel that this report is a suggestion for a design change to Stage User activation, not a statement of a vulnerability.

A flaw was found in FreeIPA versions 4.5.0 and later. Session cookies were retained in the cache after logout. An attacker could abuse this flaw if they obtain previously valid session cookies and can use this to gain access to the session.

A flaw was found in IPA, all 4.6.x versions before 4.6.7, all 4.7.x versions before 4.7.4 and all 4.8.x versions before 4.8.3, in the way that FreeIPA's batch processing API logged operations. This included passing user passwords in clear text on FreeIPA masters. Batch processing of commands with passwords as arguments or options is not performed by default in FreeIPA but is possible by third-party components. An attacker having access to system logs on FreeIPA masters could use this flaw to produce log file content with passwords exposed.

freqtrade.advisory:
Affected versions of the freqtrade package are vulnerable to path traversal due to insufficient validation of user-supplied file paths in the web UI. The web UI’s file-serving/path-resolution logic fails to properly normalize and restrict requested paths to an allowed base directory, enabling style traversal outside the intended workspace. An attacker who can trigger these web UI file requests can read (and in some deployments potentially overwrite) arbitrary files on the host, exposing secrets such as configuration files, API keys, or other sensitive data.
https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/commit/48015a9b1

freshstate.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Path Traversal. The MCP `check_rule` and `init` handlers do not validate paths for directory traversal sequences. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted paths containing traversal characters to access or manipulate files outside the intended directory.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS). The glob resolution does not detect symlink loops. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by creating circular symlinks to cause the application to enter an infinite loop, consuming CPU and potentially crashing the process.

friendlyshell.advisory: friendlyshell 1.0.3 fixes security warnings, and bugs with parsing quoted command parameters.

frigate.advisory: Frigate is a network video recorder (NVR) with real-time local object detection for IP cameras. In affected versions, when uploading a file or retrieving the filename, a user may intentionally use a large Unicode filename which would lead to an application-level denial of service. This is due to no limitation set on the length of the filename and the costly use of the Unicode normalization with the form NFKD under the hood of `secure_filename()`.

Affected versions of the frigate package are vulnerable to Improper Authorization due to missing access control on a user-deletion endpoint. The DELETE /api/users/admin endpoint is described in the advisory as accessible to an anonymous user, which allows a user with only viewer-level access to delete the admin account and other user accounts because the required role check is not enforced.

fschat.advisory: Affected versions of the fschat package are vulnerable to Denial of Service due to unbounded resource consumption in the Worker API Endpoint. The flaw resides in the api_generate function within base_model_worker.py, where commit ff66426 addressed the issue in that function but other entry points were missed, allowing the same resource exhaustion behaviour through unpatched paths. A remote attacker can submit crafted requests to the affected worker API endpoints to consume excessive resources and degrade or disrupt service availability, and a public exploit has been disclosed.

Affected versions of the lm-sys FastChat package are vulnerable to Open Redirect. The application fails to properly validate and sanitize user-supplied URL parameters, leading to unauthorized redirection. A remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by crafting a malicious URL with a specially crafted redirect parameter, resulting in users being redirected to arbitrary external websites, which can facilitate phishing attacks, malware distribution, and credential theft.

Affected versions of the lm-sys FastChat package are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS). The file upload feature fails to properly validate the length of filenames in multipart form-data requests, leading to server resource exhaustion. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted HTTP request with an excessively large filename in the form-data boundary, resulting in the server becoming overwhelmed and unavailable to legitimate users.

Affected versions of the lm-sys FastChat package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). The web server functionality fails to properly validate and sanitize user-supplied URL parameters, leading to unauthorized access to internal resources. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by crafting malicious requests to internal endpoints such as the AWS EC2 Instance Metadata Service, resulting in the exposure of sensitive credentials, including AWS IAM access keys, secret keys, and session tokens, potentially leading to full cloud infrastructure compromise.

Affected versions of the vllm-project vLLM package are vulnerable to Remote Code Execution (RCE). The MessageQueue.dequeue() API function fails to sanitize user input before deserialization, using pickle.loads to parse received socket data, directly leading to arbitrary code execution. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted malicious pickle payload to the MessageQueue service, resulting in the execution of arbitrary code with the same privileges as the vLLM application process.

Affected versions of the fschat package are vulnerable to Content Moderation Bypass due to incomplete enforcement of moderation controls across the Arena Side-by-Side View Handler. The flaw resides in the add_text function, where a prior fix in commit 34eca62 was applied to gradio_block_arena_named.py but omitted three other entry points, leaving the moderation control flow incorrect in those code paths. A remote attacker can submit crafted inputs through the unpatched side-by-side view handlers to bypass content moderation, and a public exploit has been disclosed.

The config show command in src/gac/config_cli.py printed the contents of user and project .gac.env files verbatim, without redacting secret values. gakido.advisory: Affected versions of the gakido package are vulnerable to HTTP Header Injection due to insufficient neutralization of CRLF and null byte characters in user-supplied header names and values. galaxy.advisory: Affected versions of the galaxy package are potentially vulnerable to improper access control due to a missing authentication requirement on a visualization creation endpoint. The visualization “create” API path did not consistently require an associated user, allowing requests to reach creation logic without enforcing a user-bound permission check.

galaxy-app.advisory: The Galaxy Project Galaxy version v14.10 contains a CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation vulnerability in Many templates used in the Galaxy server did not properly sanitize user's input, which would allow for cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. In this form of attack, a malicious person can create a URL which, when opened by a Galaxy user or administrator, would allow the malicious user to execute arbitrary Javascript. that can result in Arbitrary JavaScript code execution. This attack appear to be exploitable via The victim must interact with component on page witch contains injected JavaScript code.. This vulnerability appears to have been fixed in v14.10.1, v15.01.

Galaxy is an open-source platform for FAIR data analysis. Prior to version 22.05, Galaxy is vulnerable to server-side request forgery, which allows a malicious to issue arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS requests from the application server to internal hosts and read their responses. Version 22.05 contains a patch for this issue.

Galaxy is an open-source platform for data analysis. An arbitrary file read exists in Galaxy 22.01 and Galaxy 22.05 due to the switch to Gunicorn, which can be used to read any file accessible to the operating system user under which Galaxy is running. This vulnerability affects Galaxy 22.01 and higher, after the switch to gunicorn, which serve static contents directly. Additionally, the vulnerability is mitigated when using Nginx or Apache to serve /static/* contents, instead of Galaxy's internal middleware. This issue has been patched in commit `e5e6bda4f` and will be included in future releases. Users are advised to manually patch their installations. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

galaxy-importer.advisory: Galaxy-importer 0.2.15 updates 'bleach' dependency to v3.3.0 to fix a 'XSS mutation' vulnerability.

Galaxy-importer 0.4.18 includes a fix for CVE-2023-5189: A path traversal vulnerability exists in Ansible when extracting tarballs. Affected versions of GDAL's GMLAS driver are vulnerable to XML Entity Expansion attacks (Billion Laughs attack). This vulnerability can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by causing excessive resource consumption when parsing specially crafted XML files with recursive entity definitions. The attack vector involves feeding malicious XML content to the GMLAS driver, exploiting the unlimited entity expansion during parsing. The vulnerability exists in the GMLASReader class's XML parsing functions that lack restrictions on entity expansion. An attacker can exploit this by providing a crafted XML input to any application using the vulnerable GMLAS driver, potentially rendering the application unresponsive. The issue is mitigated by introducing a limit on entity expansions and aborting parsing when the limit is exceeded.

giskard-agents.advisory: Affected versions of the giskard-agents package are vulnerable to Server-side Template Injection due to the use of a non-sandboxed Jinja2 environment for user-controllable template strings. The ChatWorkflow.chat() method converts a string message argument into a MessageTemplate, and MessageTemplate.render() then passes content_template to _inline_env.from_string() even though _inline_env is created with jinja2.Environment rather than SandboxedEnvironment, allowing template expressions to access Python object internals and traverse classes.

giskard-checks.advisory: Affected versions of the giskard-checks package are vulnerable to Remote Code Execution due to unsandboxed Jinja2 template rendering of the rule parameter. The ConformityCheck class in conformity.py at line 59 passes the rule string directly to Jinja2's default Template() constructor and calls render(), so any template expressions embedded in rule definitions are evaluated at runtime without sandboxing. An attacker who can control a check definition, for example through a shared project file or externally contributed configuration that is later executed by a developer, can embed malicious template expressions in the rule parameter to achieve arbitrary code execution within the developer's environment.

Affected versions of the giskard-checks package are vulnerable to Denial of Service due to unbounded evaluation of user-supplied regular expression patterns. The RegexMatching check in text_matching.py at line 457 passes the pattern parameter directly to Python's re.search() with no timeout, complexity guard, or pattern validation, so a crafted pattern can trigger catastrophic backtracking in the regex engine. An attacker who can control either the regex pattern or the text being matched can cause the process to hang indefinitely, consuming CPU and denying service to other operations, which is particularly impactful in automated environments such as CI/CD pipelines.

gitpython.advisory:
Gitpython 3.1.27 includes a fix for a REDoS vulnerability.
https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/commit/75f4f63ab3856a552f06082aabf98845b5fa21e3

Gitpython 3.1.30 includes a fix for CVE-2022-24439: Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability due to improper user input validation, which makes it possible to inject a maliciously crafted remote URL into the clone command. Exploiting this vulnerability is possible because the library makes external calls to git without sufficient sanitization of input arguments.
https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/commit/2625ed9fc074091c531c27ffcba7902771130261
GitPython before 3.1.32 does not block insecure non-multi options in clone and clone_from. NOTE: this issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2022-24439.

GitPython affected versions are vulnerable to Path Traversal (CWE-22). This vulnerability allows an attacker to potentially read arbitrary files from the system, which could lead to information disclosure or denial of service. The attack vector involves manipulating reference names to include path traversal sequences. The vulnerable functionality was in the handling of reference paths, which didn't properly validate user input. The initial fix was implemented with further security improvements in subsequent versions.

GitPython 3.1.41 fixes a vulnerability (CVE-2024-22190) involving an untrusted search path issue on Windows, which could allow execution of malicious git.exe or bash.exe from untrusted repositories. This update addresses the incomplete fix from CVE-2023-40590. 
#It only affects Windows users
https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-2mqj-m65w-jghx

Affected versions of the GitPython package are vulnerable to Argument Injection due to the unsafe-option check being applied to multi_options before the value is transformed by shlex.split. In _clone() at git/repo/base.py line 1383, multi_options is first joined and passed through shlex.split, but check_unsafe_options at line 1390 validates the original list rather than the post-split tokens, so a single element such as '--branch main --config core.hooksPath=/x' passes the prefix check yet expands at line 1392 into separate --config and core.hooksPath tokens that Git honors during clone. An attacker who can influence multi_options can smuggle dangerous Git options past the validator and apply arbitrary configuration directives, such as core.hooksPath, causing Git to execute attacker-controlled hook scripts during the clone operation and achieve arbitrary command execution.

Affected versions of the GitPython package are vulnerable to Argument Injection due to the unsafe-option check being applied to multi_options before the value is transformed by shlex.split. In _clone() at git/repo/base.py line 1383, multi_options is first joined and passed through shlex.split, but check_unsafe_options at line 1390 validates the original list rather than the post-split tokens, so a single element such as '--branch main --config core.hooksPath=/x' passes the prefix check yet expands at line 1392 into separate --config and core.hooksPath tokens that Git honors during clone. An attacker who can influence multi_options can smuggle dangerous Git options past the validator and apply arbitrary configuration directives, such as core.hooksPath, causing Git to execute attacker-controlled hook scripts during the clone operation and achieve arbitrary command execution.

Gitpython 3.1.33 includes a fix for CVE-2023-40590: Untrusted search path on Windows systems leading to arbitrary code execution.
https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-wfm5-v35h-vwf4

Affected versions of the GitPython package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to insufficient validation of attacker-controlled reference paths before filesystem write, rename, and delete operations. Although SymbolicReference._check_ref_name_valid() rejects traversal sequences, the SymbolicReference.create, Reference.create, SymbolicReference.set_reference, SymbolicReference.rename, and SymbolicReference.delete methods construct filesystem paths from supplied ref names without enforcing the repository boundary. An attacker who can supply a crafted reference name to an application using GitPython can write, overwrite, move, or delete arbitrary files outside the repository's .git directory, resulting in Arbitrary File Write and Arbitrary File Deletion.

Affected versions of the GitPython package are vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via Newline Injection due to GitConfigParser.set_value() passing values to Python's configparser without validating for embedded newline characters. GitPython's _write() method converts embedded newlines into indented continuation lines, but Git still accepts an indented [core] stanza as a valid section header, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary Git configuration directives such as core.hooksPath into .git/config. An attacker who can control values passed to config_writer().set_value() can point core.hooksPath to an attacker-controlled directory, causing any subsequent Git operation that invokes hooks (commit, merge, checkout) to execute arbitrary scripts.

Affected versions of the GitPython package are vulnerable to Remote Code Execution (RCE) due to incomplete input validation in the set_value() method of GitConfigParser. The patch for CVE-2026-42215 validates newline characters only in the value parameter, while the section and option parameters are passed to configparser without any newline sanitisation, allowing injection of arbitrary section headers into .git/config. An attacker who controls the section argument can inject a forged [core] section with a hooksPath directive pointing to an attacker-controlled directory, leading to arbitrary code execution when any git hook is triggered.

Affected versions of the GitPython package are vulnerable to Command Injection due to the unsafe-option allowlist being bypassed by equivalent Python keyword arguments. While GitPython's check_unsafe_options validator blocks dangerous Git CLI flags such as --upload-pack and --receive-pack by default, the corresponding upload_pack and receive_pack Python kwargs are accepted by Repo.clone_from(), Remote.fetch(), Remote.pull(), and Remote.push() are translated into the same Git invocation without passing through the unsafe-option check defined in git/repo/base.py and git/remote.py. An attacker who can supply attacker-controlled kwargs to these GitPython APIs can therefore specify arbitrary helper-command paths via upload_pack or receive_pack and achieve arbitrary command execution even when allow_unsafe_options is left at its default value of False.

glance.advisory: The image parser in OpenStack Cinder 7.0.2 and 8.0.0 through 8.1.1; Glance before 11.0.1 and 12.0.0; and Nova before 12.0.4 and 13.0.0 does not properly limit qemu-img calls, which might allow attackers to cause a denial of service (memory and disk consumption) via a crafted disk image.

The v1 API in OpenStack Glance Essex (2012.1), Folsom (2012.2), and Grizzly, when using the single-tenant Swift or S3 store, reports the location field, which allows remote authenticated users to obtain the operator's backend credentials via a request for a cached image.

An SSRF issue was discovered in OpenStack Glance before Newton. The 'copy_from' feature in the Image Service API v1 allowed an attacker to perform masked network port scans. With v1, it is possible to create images with a URL such as 'localhost:22'. This could then allow an attacker to enumerate internal network details while appearing masked, since the scan would appear to originate from the Glance Image service.
The API before 2.1 in OpenStack Image Registry and Delivery Service (Glance) makes it easier for local users to inject images into arbitrary tenants by adding the tenant as a member of the image.

Glance 23.0.1, 24.1.1 and 25.0.0 include a fix for CVE-2022-47951: An issue was discovered in OpenStack Cinder before 19.1.2, 20.x before 20.0.2, and 21.0.0; Glance before 23.0.1, 24.x before 24.1.1, and 25.0.0; and Nova before 24.1.2, 25.x before 25.0.2, and 26.0.0. By supplying a specially created VMDK flat image that references a specific backing file path, an authenticated user may convince systems to return a copy of that file's contents from the server, resulting in unauthorized access to potentially sensitive data.

A security flaw in affected versions of OpenStack Glance allows arbitrary file access via custom QCOW2 external data. An authenticated user can supply a crafted QCOW2 image that references a specific data file path, convincing systems to return a copy of that file's contents from the server. This results in unauthorized access to potentially sensitive data.

Affected versions of the OpenStack Glance package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) due to improper URL validation during image import redirects. The web-download and glance-download image import methods, as well as the optional ovf_process image import plugin, do not correctly prevent redirected requests from reaching disallowed destinations after an initial URL validation check.
The image signature algorithm in OpenStack Glance 11.0.0 allows remote attackers to bypass the signature verification process via a crafted image, which triggers an MD5 collision.

OpenStack Image Registry and Delivery Service (Glance) Folsom, Grizzly before 2013.1.4, and Havana before 2013.2, when the download_image policy is configured, does not properly restrict access to cached images, which allows remote authenticated users to read otherwise restricted images via an image UUID.

A flaw was found in openstack-glance. This issue could allow a remote, authenticated attacker to tamper with images, compromising the integrity of virtual machines created using these modified images.
https://wiki.openstack.org/wiki/OSSN/OSSN-0090

OpenStack Image Registry and Delivery Service (Glance) 2013.2 through 2013.2.1 and Icehouse before icehouse-2 logs a URL containing the Swift store backend password when authentication fails and WARNING level logging is enabled, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information by reading the log.

OpenStack Image Registry and Delivery Service (Glance) before 2013.2.4, 2014.x before 2014.1.3, and Juno before Juno-3, when using the V2 API, does not properly enforce the image_size_cap configuration option, which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (disk consumption) by uploading a large image.

The V2 API in OpenStack Image Registry and Delivery Service (Glance) before 2014.1.4 and 2014.2.x before 2014.2.2 allows remote authenticated users to read or delete arbitrary files via a full pathname in a filesystem: URL in the image location property.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2014-9493.

OpenStack Image Registry and Delivery Service (Glance) 2014.2 through 2014.2.2 does not properly remove images, which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (disk consumption) by creating a large number of images using the task v2 API and then deleting them before the uploads finish, a different vulnerability than CVE-2015-1881.

OpenStack Image Registry and Delivery Service (Glance) 2014.2 through 2014.2.2 does not properly remove images, which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (disk consumption) by creating a large number of images using the task v2 API and then deleting them, a different vulnerability than CVE-2014-9684.

OpenStack Glance before 2015.1.1 (kilo) allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (disk consumption) by repeatedly using the import task flow API to create images and then deleting them.

OpenStack Glance 2014.2.x through 2014.2.1, 2014.1.3, and earlier allows remote authenticated users to bypass the storage quota and cause a denial of service (disk consumption) by deleting an image in the saving state.

A vulnerability was found in Openstack Glance. No limits are enforced within the Glance image service for both v1 and v2 `/images` API POST method for authenticated users, resulting in possible denial of service attacks through database table saturation.

OpenStack Image Service (Glance) before 2014.2.4 (juno) and 2015.1.x before 2015.1.2 (kilo) allow remote authenticated users to change the status of their images and bypass access restrictions via the HTTP x-image-meta-status header to images/*.

OpenStack Image Service (Glance) before 2014.2.4 (juno) and 2015.1.x before 2015.1.2 (kilo) allows remote authenticated users to bypass the storage quota and cause a denial of service (disk consumption) by deleting images that are being uploaded using a token that expires during the process. NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2014-9623.

OpenStack Image Service (Glance) before 2015.1.3 (kilo) and 11.0.x before 11.0.2 (liberty), when show_multiple_locations is enabled, allow remote authenticated users to change image status and upload new image data by removing the last location of an image.

store/swift.py in OpenStack Glance Essex (2012.1), Folsom (2012.2) before 2012.2.3, and Grizzly, when in Swift single tenant mode, logs the Swift endpoint's user name and password in cleartext when the endpoint is misconfigured or unusable, allows remote authenticated users to obtain sensitive information by reading the error messages.

The v2 API in OpenStack Glance Grizzly, Folsom (2012.2), and Essex (2012.1) allows remote authenticated users to delete arbitrary non-protected images via an image deletion request.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2012-4573.

The v1 API in OpenStack Glance Grizzly, Folsom (2012.2), and Essex (2012.1) allows remote authenticated users to delete arbitrary non-protected images via an image deletion request, a different vulnerability than CVE-2012-5482.

The Sheepdog backend in OpenStack Image Registry and Delivery Service (Glance) 2013.2 before 2013.2.4 and icehouse before icehouse-rc2 allows remote authenticated users with permission to insert or modify an image to execute arbitrary commands via a crafted location.

The V2 API in OpenStack Image Registry and Delivery Service (Glance) before 2014.2.2 and 2014.1.4 allows remote authenticated users to read or delete arbitrary files via a full pathname in a file: URL in the image location property.

The import task action in OpenStack Image Service (Glance) 2015.1.x before 2015.1.2 (kilo), when using the V2 API, allows remote authenticated users to read arbitrary files via a crafted backing file for a qcow2 image.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Server-Side Template Injection. The Jinja2 templating engine is configured without autoescape enabled (Bandit B701). An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by injecting malicious template syntax into user-controlled input to execute arbitrary code or access sensitive data on the server.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS). HTTP requests are made without configuring timeouts (Bandit B113). An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by causing the application to make requests to a slow or unresponsive server, causing the application to hang indefinitely and become unavailable.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure. The application logs sensitive information in cleartext. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by gaining access to log files to obtain sensitive data.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to SQL Injection due to improper neutralization of single quotes in exported string values. In glances/exports/glances_timescaledb/init.py, the normalize() method wraps string values with f"'{value}'" and list items with f"'{v}'" without escaping embedded quotes, and those values are concatenated into an INSERT statement that is executed directly with cur.execute().

Affected versions of the glances package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to missing authentication and secret filtering in configuration API responses. The /api/4/config endpoint in glances/outputs/glances_restful_api.py calls self.config.as_dict(), and the as_dict() method in glances/config.py returns every configuration section and option from glances.conf without redacting sensitive values such as database passwords, API tokens, JWT signing keys, and SSL key passwords; when self.args.password is not set, the API router is created without the self.authentication dependency.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to exposure of reusable downstream authentication credentials in API responses. In Central Browser mode, the /api/4/serverslist endpoint returns raw server objects from GlancesServersList.get_servers_list(), and the get_uri() and __update_stats() logic adds a uri field containing embedded HTTP Basic credentials derived from the saved Glances password hash; when the front Glances instance is started without --password, the route is left unauthenticated.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to missing host validation on the main REST/WebUI FastAPI application. The glances/outputs/glances_restful_api.py module creates the main FastAPI(...) app for the REST API, WebUI, and /token routes without TrustedHostMiddleware or any equivalent allowlist enforcement for the HTTP Host header, while glances/main.py binds the service to 0.0.0.0 by default.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to incomplete redaction of sensitive command-line arguments. The glances/outputs/glances_restful_api.py module exposes _api_args and _api_args_item, which return vars(self.args) directly through the /api/v4/args and /api/v4/args/{item} endpoints without sanitizing fields such as password, snmp_community, snmp_user, snmp_auth, username, and conf_file.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to Command Injection due to unsafe splitting of Mustache-rendered action command templates on shell metacharacters. In glances/actions.py, action templates are rendered with user-controllable fields such as {{name}}, then passed to secure_popen() in glances/secure.py, which splits the fully rendered command on &&, > and | before executing each segment, causing attacker-supplied process names, container names, or mount points to be treated as command operators rather than data.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to Cross-Origin Credential Theft due to an overly permissive default CORS configuration. In glances/outputs/glances_restful_api.py, Glances configures Starlette CORSMiddleware with allow_origins=["*"] and allow_credentials=True, which causes the middleware to reflect an attacker-controlled Origin header and allows cross-origin JavaScript to read responses from endpoints such as /api/4/all, /api/4/config, and /api/4/args.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to improper trust of Zeroconf-advertised hostnames during Central Browser autodiscovery. In Central Browser mode, glances/servers_list_dynamic.py stores both the discovered ip and the advertised name, but glances/servers_list.py:get_uri() and glances/client_browser.py use server['name'] for both password lookup and credential-bearing URI construction, causing Glances to bind saved credentials to attacker-controlled service names instead of the discovered IP address.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to authentication being disabled by default for the web server REST API. When Glances is started with glances -w, glances/outputs/glances_restful_api.py sets self._password = None, creates the APIRouter without the Depends(self.authentication) dependency, and binds to 0.0.0.0, while glances/plugins/processlist/__init__.py exposes unsanitized cmdline values through /api/4/processlist.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to SQL Injection due to unparameterized SQL identifier construction. In glances/exports/glances_duckdb/__init__.py, the DuckDB export module builds CREATE TABLE and INSERT INTO statements with f-strings in the export() path, and creation_list is populated from plugin_stats keys in update() without quoting or safely composing table and column identifiers.

Affected versions of the glances package are vulnerable to CQL Injection due to unsanitised interpolation of configuration values into Cassandra Query Language statements in the Cassandra export module at glances/exports/glances_cassandra/init.py. The keyspace, table, and replication_factor values are taken directly from glances.conf and inserted via f-string formatting into CREATE KEYSPACE, CREATE TABLE, and INSERT INTO statements without identifier validation, permitting qualified identifiers such as attacker_ks.captured_stats to alter the target of every write. An attacker with write access to glances.conf can redirect all exported monitoring data, including CPU, memory, network, and disk I/O metrics, to an attacker-controlled keyspace, resulting in silent data exfiltration and loss of legitimate monitoring data.

Affected versions of the glances package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery due to missing validation of the public_api configuration parameter in the IP plugin. The value of public_api in glances/plugins/ip/init.py is read from configuration and passed directly to ThreadPublicIpAddress and ultimately to urlopen_auth() in glances/globals.py, with no restriction on URL scheme, hostname, or destination IP range, and any configured public_username and public_password are automatically attached as a Basic Authorization header. An attacker able to modify glances.conf can direct outbound requests to internal services, loopback addresses, private network ranges, or cloud metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254, resulting in Information Disclosure, credential leakage to attacker-controlled servers, and injection of attacker-supplied data into the /api/4/ip response.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to CORS Misconfiguration due to the web server returning Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for its unauthenticated REST API at/api/4/*. Because no authentication is required by default and the permissive CORS header permits cross-origin reads from any origin, endpoints such as /api/4/all return extensive host information, including the process list, hostname, OS, CPU details, memory and disk usage, network interfaces, and IP addresses to any requesting page. A remote attacker can host a malicious website that, when visited by a user running Glances in web mode, performs cross-origin fetches against the local Glances instance and exfiltrates sensitive system information, enabling reconnaissance and Information Disclosure without any user interaction beyond visiting the page.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to a permissive cross-origin policy on the XML-RPC server. In glances/server.py, GlancesXMLRPCHandler.send_my_headers() sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every response, and the XML-RPC handler accepts POST requests with Content-Type: text/plain, allowing browser-issued CORS simple requests to invoke methods such as getAll(), getPlugin(), getAllPlugins(), getAllLimits(), and getAllViews() without a preflight check.

Affected versions of the Glances package are vulnerable to Command Injection due to unsafe execution of dynamic configuration values enclosed in backticks. The Config.get_value() method in glances/config.py detects backtick-delimited substrings in configuration entries and passes them directly to system_exec() in glances/globals.py, which executes the supplied command without validation or restriction.

glpi-py.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to SQL Injection. The `DBmysql::query()` method allows execution of SQL queries without enforcing safe query construction practices. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by injecting malicious SQL syntax through user-controlled input that is passed to queries using this method to execute arbitrary database commands or access unauthorized data.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure. The autocompletion feature is enabled by default on search fields without requiring explicit authorization. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by accessing the autocompletion functionality to enumerate sensitive field values that should not be exposed.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Authorization Bypass. The API access control mechanism trusts the `X-Forwarded-For` header value for making authorization decisions. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by setting a spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` header to bypass IP-based access controls and gain unauthorized access to the API.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). POST requests to `/ajax/` endpoints do not require CSRF token validation. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by tricking an authenticated user into visiting a malicious page that submits crafted requests to perform unauthorized actions on behalf of the victim.

gluoncv.advisory: A vulnerability in the ImageClassificationDataset.from_csv() API of the dmlc/gluon-cv repository, version 0.10.0, allows for arbitrary file write. The function downloads and extracts tar.gz files from URLs without proper sanitization, making it susceptible to a TarSlip vulnerability. Attackers can exploit this by crafting malicious tar files that, when extracted, can overwrite files on the victim's system via path traversal or faked symlinks.

gmaps-mcp.advisory: Affected versions of the gmaps-mcp package are vulnerable to Missing Authentication due to the HTTP transport skipping authentication entirely when the API key is configured as a blank value, which is the default shipped configuration. Any unauthenticated caller who discovers the server's public URL can invoke all six MCP tools and generate live, billed Google Maps API requests against the operator's key without providing an X-API-Key header. An attacker can exploit this to exhaust the operator's Google Maps API quota and incur high financial costs, with the $200 monthly free credit exhaustible in approximately three hours at sustained request rates.

gnosis-mcp.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). The application does not block requests to private/internal IP addresses (127.x, 10.x, 192.168.x, ::1) or cloud metadata endpoints, and does not validate redirect targets. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by providing URLs that resolve to internal network resources or cloud metadata endpoints to access sensitive internal services or retrieve cloud credentials.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insecure File Permissions. Cache files are created without restrictive permissions, allowing other users on shared systems to read potentially sensitive cached data. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by reading cache files on a shared system to obtain sensitive information from crawled content.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS). The `fetch_page` function does not enforce response size limits and the BFS discovery queue has no cap on size. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by serving excessively large responses or triggering unbounded URL discovery to exhaust server memory.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS). The sitemap parser does not enforce size limits on XML input, allowing billion-laughs-style XML expansion attacks. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by providing a malicious sitemap containing recursive entity definitions to exhaust server memory and CPU.

goodmap.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) due to improper usage of CSRF protection mechanisms. CSRF protection was not correctly implemented for multipart/form-data, potentially allowing malicious requests to be processed without proper validation. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by tricking a user into executing unwanted actions on a web application where they are authenticated, leading to unauthorized operations being performed on behalf of the user.

google-adk.advisory: Affected versions of the Google-ADK package are vulnerable to Remote Code Execution due to Missing Authentication on exposed administrative functionality in the ADK web server. An unauthenticated remote attacker can reach code-execution pathways in the ADK instance on Python (OSS), Cloud Run, and GKE deployments, permitting injection of arbitrary code without any prior authorisation. Exploitation enables the attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server hosting the ADK instance, resulting in full compromise of the host process.

google-appengine.advisory: The sandbox environment in the Google App Engine Python SDK before 1.5.4 does not properly prevent use of the os module, which allows local users to bypass intended access restrictions and execute arbitrary commands via a file_blob_storage.os reference within the code parameter to _ah/admin/interactive/execute, a different vulnerability than CVE-2011-1364.

The sandbox environment in the Google App Engine Python SDK before 1.5.4 does not properly prevent os.popen calls, which allows local users to bypass intended access restrictions and execute arbitrary commands via a dev_appserver.RestrictedPathFunction._original_os reference within the code parameter to _ah/admin/interactive/execute, a different vulnerability than CVE-2011-1364.

The FakeFile implementation in the sandbox environment in the Google App Engine Python SDK before 1.5.4 does not properly control the opening of files, which allows local users to bypass intended access restrictions and create arbitrary files via ALLOWED_MODES and ALLOWED_DIRS changes within the code parameter to _ah/admin/interactive/execute, a different vulnerability than CVE-2011-1364.

Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in _ah/admin/interactive/execute (aka the Interactive Console) in the SDK Console (aka Admin Console) in the Google App Engine Python SDK before 1.5.4 allows remote attackers to hijack the authentication of administrators for requests that execute arbitrary Python code via the code parameter.

google-cloud-aiplatform.advisory: Affected versions of the google-cloud-aiplatform package are vulnerable to Remote Code Execution due to predictable Cloud Storage bucket naming for Vertex AI Experiments. Vertex AI Experiments relies on a deterministic bucket naming scheme and does not sufficiently ensure that the bucket it uses was created and controlled by the intended tenant, enabling “bucket squatting” by leveraging an already-existing bucket with the expected name.

Affected versions of the google-cloud-aiplatform package are vulnerable to Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to improper escaping of user-controlled model evaluation results and dataset JSON content before rendering it as HTML. The vulnerability exists in the _genai/_evals_visualization component, which processes model evaluation results or dataset JSON data containing script escape sequences without correctly neutralizing them, allowing attacker-supplied content to be interpreted as executable JavaScript.

gpt-pilot.advisory: Affected versions of the gpt-pilot package are vulnerable to Command Injection due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input during project execution. The Executor.run() method passes user-provided free-text input directly to asyncio.create_subprocess_shell() without sanitisation when prompting the user to confirm or modify a command. An attacker can replace the intended command with arbitrary shell commands, achieving Remote Code Execution with the privileges of the GPT-Pilot process.

gradio.advisory: Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to incorrect absolute-path detection on Windows when running under Python 3.13+. Gradio’s “safe” path-joining logic relies on os.path.isabs, but Python 3.13+ changed its Windows behaviour so that root-relative inputs like /windows/win.ini are no longer treated as absolute paths, allowing attacker-controlled paths to bypass the intended directory restrictions.

Gradio 3.19.1 includes a fix for CVE-2023-25823: When using Gradio's share links (i.e. creating a Gradio app and then setting 'share=True'), a private SSH key is sent to any user that connects to the Gradio machine, which means that a user could access other users' shared Gradio demos. From there, other exploits are possible depending on the level of access/exposure the Gradio app provides. This issue is patched in version 3.13.1, however, users are recommended to update to 3.19.1 or later where the FRP solution has been properly tested.
https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/security/advisories/GHSA-3x5j-9vwr-8rr5

Gradio 4.10.0 includes a fix for a SSRF vulnerability on '/file=' route.
https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/pull/6794

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) due to insufficient validation of the file parameter in GET requests. The vulnerability allows attackers to manipulate the file parameter to make requests to internal network resources, with the application's response behaviour revealing information about port status through the presence or absence of Location headers and error messages.

Gradio has a vulnerability in versions prior to 4.11.0, allowing file traversal attacks. Attackers could access arbitrary files on a machine running a Gradio app with a public URL, given they knew the file paths. This issue has been fixed in version 4.11.0.
https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/security/advisories/GHSA-6qm2-wpxq-7qh2

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Read due to insufficient authorization controls on the /component_server endpoint. The vulnerability stems from the endpoint's lack of proper authorization checks, allowing attackers to invoke arbitrary methods on the Component class, specifically targeting the move_resource_to_block_cache method of the underlying Block class with malicious parameters.
Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in GitHub repository gradio-app/gradio prior to main.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) due to insufficient validation of user-supplied URLs in the /proxy route. The vulnerability exists in the build_proxy_request function's inadequate checking of safe URLs, allowing attackers to manipulate the self.replica_urls set through the X-Direct-Url header in requests to the / and /config routes.

A command injection vulnerability exists in the deploy+test-visual.yml workflow of the gradio-app/gradio repository, due to improper neutralization of special elements used in a command. This vulnerability allows attackers to execute unauthorized commands, potentially leading to unauthorized modification of the base repository or secrets exfiltration. The issue arises from the unsafe handling of GitHub context information within a `run` operation, where expressions inside `${{ }}` are evaluated and substituted before script execution. Remediation involves setting untrusted input values to intermediate environment variables to prevent direct influence on script generation.

Gradio version 4.19.1 introduces security enhancements to protect against timing attacks that could potentially guess Gradio passwords.
https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/commit/e329f1fd38935213fe0e73962e8cbd5d3af6e87b

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Observable Response Discrepancy due to the use of a direct comparison operation in the login function within routes.py. The vulnerability stems from the authentication mechanism using app.auth[username] == password for credential validation, which creates measurable timing differences in response times based on the correctness of submitted credentials.
Gradio - Arbitrary File Access

Gradio affected versions allow credential leakage on Windows.
# This only affects Windows users

Gradio version 4.22.0 addresses a race condition that impacted the synchronization between state and loading status updates. This fix is crucial for preventing potential vulnerabilities that could disrupt service, such as denial of service (DoS) attacks.
https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/commit/84f81fec9287b041203a141bbf2852720f7d199c

A local file inclusion vulnerability exists in the JSON component of gradio-app/gradio. The vulnerability arises from improper input validation in the `postprocess()` function within `gradio/components/json_component.py`, where a user-controlled string is parsed as JSON. If the parsed JSON object contains a `path` key, the specified file is moved to a temporary directory, making it possible to retrieve it later via the `/file=..` endpoint. This issue is due to the `processing_utils.move_files_to_cache()` function traversing any object passed to it, looking for a dictionary with a `path` key, and then copying the specified file to a temporary directory. The vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker to read files on the remote system, posing a significant security risk.

An open redirect vulnerability exists in the latest version of gradio-app/gradio. The vulnerability allows an attacker to redirect users to a malicious website by URL encoding. This can be exploited by sending a crafted request to the application, which results in a 302 redirect to an attacker-controlled site.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Improper Authorization and Origin Validation Error due to missing Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) origin validation when a cookie is present. The Gradio server’s CORS logic conditionally bypasses origin validation in the presence of a cookie, enabling requests to `CustomCORSMiddleware` or equivalent CORS-handling modules to proceed without verifying the request origin. An attacker can exploit this by luring a Gradio user (with an active session) to visit a malicious website that sends forged requests—these may include uploading files, stealing authentication tokens, or accessing user data—resulting in unauthorized actions on the local Gradio instance.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to the enable_monitoring flag not properly disabling monitoring when set to False. The gradio package does not prevent access to the /monitoring endpoint even when enable_monitoring=False is configured, resulting in the monitoring dashboard remaining accessible. An attacker who knows or discovers the endpoint path can request /monitoring and view potentially sensitive application analytics even in contexts where monitoring was intended to be disabled.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to a Timing Attack due to non-constant-time comparison of hash values. The analytics_dashboard function performs a standard (non-constant-time) hash comparison, allowing variations in response time to leak information about each byte of the hash. An attacker able to issue repeated requests to the analytics dashboard can measure timing differences to infer the correct hash value byte-by-byte, potentially gaining unauthorized access to the analytics dashboard.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory (‘one-level read path traversal’ in the `/custom_component` endpoint). The `/custom_component` endpoint accepts a user-controlled file path and fails to properly restrict directory traversal sequences, allowing traversal into adjacent directories. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a request with a manipulated path to read and leak the source code of custom Gradio components, potentially exposing proprietary or sensitive code.
A local file include could be remotely triggered in Gradio due to a vulnerable user-supplied JSON value in an API request.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation (CORS misconfiguration) due to the acceptance of the "null" origin in the localhost_aliases variable. The CORS origin validation logic in gradio includes `"null"` as a permitted origin when the server is deployed locally, allowing origins with a `null` value—such as sandboxed iframes—to bypass origin restrictions. An attacker can exploit this by embedding a page in a sandboxed iframe that issues unauthorized requests to the Gradio server, potentially causing disclosure of user authentication tokens or uploading files in contexts using basic authentication.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to the missing encryption of sensitive data when using insecure communication between the Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) client and server under the `share=True` configuration. The FRP client-server communication path does not enforce HTTPS, leaving the connection unencrypted and permitting interception or manipulation of files uploaded and data exchanged during Gradio demo sessions. An attacker can exploit this by intercepting network traffic between the FRP client and server when `share=True` is used, enabling them to read uploaded files and modify responses, resulting in the compromise of confidentiality and integrity of the demo session.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory via the `is_in_or_equal` function. The `is_in_or_equal` function in gradio incorrectly uses an inadequate path validation approach—such as relying on `os.path.commonprefix`—which can be bypassed by crafted `..` (parent directory) sequences that circumvent directory constraints. An attacker can exploit this by supplying malicious input that escapes the intended directory boundary, potentially granting access to restricted files on the host filesystem and disclosing sensitive information, though exploitation complexity is relatively high.

Gradio affected versions are vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of another user. This vulnerability is due to improper handling of SVG files in the gr.Image and gr.Gallery components. The issue was addressed in commit 890eaa3, which implemented secure SVG display.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to a Race Condition due to improper synchronization in the update_root_in_config function. The update_root_in_config function within the Gradio configuration module allows concurrent execution that enables modification of the root URL without atomicity or locking. An attacker racing multiple requests to that function could redirect frontend user traffic to a malicious server, allowing interception of sensitive information such as authentication credentials or uploaded files.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) due to insufficient validation in the `async_save_url_to_cache` function. The `/queue/join` endpoint invokes `async_save_url_to_cache` with a user-controlled URL parameter without restricting internal or local network targets, enabling arbitrary HTTP requests. An attacker can exploit this by supplying a malicious URL to force the Gradio server to contact internal services or fetch unintended resources—which are then stored locally—potentially leading to internal network reconnaissance or injection of malicious files.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Improper Authorization and Origin Validation Error due to missing Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) origin validation when a cookie is present. The Gradio server’s CORS logic conditionally bypasses origin validation in the presence of a cookie, enabling requests to `CustomCORSMiddleware` or equivalent CORS-handling modules to proceed without verifying the request origin. An attacker can exploit this by luring a Gradio user (with an active session) to visit a malicious website that sends forged requests—these may include uploading files, stealing authentication tokens, or accessing user data—resulting in unauthorized actions on the local Gradio instance.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation (lack of integrity check) due to the omission of checksum or signature verification on the downloaded FRP client. The component responsible for downloading the FRP client within Gradio’s sharing mechanism fails to validate the authenticity of the binary, relying solely on external sources without verifying integrity. An attacker able to compromise or manipulate the remote URL hosting the FRP client can supply a tampered executable, which Gradio will accept and run, potentially resulting in the execution of malicious code on systems using the hosting functionality.

Affected versions of the Gradio package are vulnerable to a Race Condition (CWE-362). This vulnerability allows attackers to manipulate the shared configuration object, leading to the modification of the root URL in other users' configurations. Attackers can exploit this by sending requests with malicious headers, such as X-Forwarded-Host, to inject a fake root URL into the application's configuration. The vulnerable functions are update_root_in_config and route handlers that access and modify blocks.config without proper isolation. To mitigate this issue, update to the version of Gradio where each request operates on a deep copy of the configuration, ensuring that modifications in one request do not affect others.

A vulnerability in the gradio-app/gradio repository, version git 67e4044, allows for path traversal on Windows OS. The implementation of the blocked_path functionality, which is intended to disallow users from reading certain files, is flawed. Specifically, while the application correctly blocks access to paths like 'C:/tmp/secret.txt', it fails to block access when using NTFS Alternate Data Streams (ADS) syntax, such as 'C:/tmp/secret.txt::$DATA'. This flaw can lead to unauthorized reading of blocked file paths.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attacks. An attacker can supply specially crafted HTML input that causes the remove_html_tags function to consume excessive CPU resources, leading to service unavailability. The vulnerability exists in the HTML_TAG_RE regex within gradio/utils.py. This issue has been addressed in commit eb85edf, which updates the regex to prevent excessive backtracking.

Gradio is an open-source Python package that allows quick building of demos and web application for machine learning models, API, or any arbitrary Python function. Prior to version 5.31.0, an arbitrary file copy vulnerability in Gradio's flagging feature allows unauthenticated attackers to copy any readable file from the server's filesystem. While attackers can't read these copied files, they can cause DoS by copying large files (like /dev/urandom) to fill disk space. This issue has been patched in version 5.31.0.

Affected versions of the Gradio package are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) due to insufficient resource limits in the multipart parser. The `GradioMultiPartParser` class fails to enforce size limits on HTTP headers during multipart form data processing, allowing unbounded header accumulation. 

A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multipart requests with excessively large headers, causing memory exhaustion and denial of service. Additionally, the parser performed blocking file system operations using `os.stat()` during file upload processing, which could be exploited to cause performance degradation.

The vulnerability was fixed by implementing a maximum header size limit of 8KB (`max_header_size = 1024 * 8`) and removing the blocking `os.stat()` call in favour of tracking file sizes in memory during upload processing.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Open Redirect due to accepting an unvalidated _target_url query parameter in its OAuth redirect logic. The _redirect_to_target() function reads _target_url from request.query_params and passes it directly to RedirectResponse, impacting the /logout and /login/callback endpoints when OAuth is enabled (for example, Hugging Face Spaces using gr.LoginButton).

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) because they trust an attacker-controlled proxy_url value from a remotely loaded Space configuration. When gr.load() calls Blocks.from_config() (in gradio/external.py) and processes the fetched config, gradio/blocks.py adds config["proxy_url"] directly into self.proxy_urls, and the built-in /proxy={url_path:path} reverse_proxy route in gradio/routes.py only validates requests by checking whether the requested URL host matches a host in that allowlist.

Gradio 3.34.0 includes a fix for a path traversal vulnerability.
https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/pull/4370
https://github.com/gradio-app/gradio/security/advisories/GHSA-3qqg-pgqq-3695

A Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in the gradio-app/gradio, specifically within the `/queue/join` endpoint and the `save_url_to_cache` function. The vulnerability arises when the `path` value, obtained from the user and expected to be a URL, is used to make an HTTP request without sufficient validation checks. This flaw allows an attacker to send crafted requests that could lead to unauthorized access to the local network or the AWS metadata endpoint, thereby compromising the security of internal servers.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Open Redirect due to improper validation of user-supplied input in URL handling. The application processes URLs without adequately verifying their destination, allowing maliciously crafted redirect parameters to bypass security controls.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery due to the save_url_to_cache function imposing no restrictions on supplied URLs. The gr.DownloadButton function in the gradio module uses save_url_to_cache to fetch arbitrary URLs without validating their schemes or destinations, enabling requests to internal or local resources. An attacker able to trigger gr.DownloadButton can supply a crafted URL that causes gradio to retrieve local files or internal services, disclosing sensitive information or local resources to the attacker.

A vulnerability in the file upload process of gradio-app/gradio version @gradio/video@0.10.2 allows for a Denial of Service (DoS) attack. An attacker can append a large number of characters to the end of a multipart boundary, causing the system to continuously process each character and issue warnings. This can render Gradio inaccessible for extended periods, disrupting services and causing significant downtime.
Gradio v3.27.0 was discovered to contain an arbitrary file upload vulnerability via the /upload interface.

Gradio is an open source framework for building interactive machine learning models and demos. In versions prior to 2.5.0 there is a vulnerability that affects anyone who creates and publicly shares Gradio interfaces. File paths are not restricted and users who receive a Gradio link can access any files on the host computer if they know the file names or file paths. This is limited only by the host operating system. Paths are opened in read only mode. The problem has been patched in gradio 2.5.0.

`gradio` is an open source framework for building interactive machine learning models and demos. Prior to version 2.8.11, `gradio` suffers from Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File. The `gradio` library has a flagging functionality which saves input/output data into a CSV file on the developer's computer. This can allow a user to save arbitrary text into the CSV file, such as commands. If a program like MS Excel opens such a file, then it automatically runs these commands, which could lead to arbitrary commands running on the user's computer. The problem has been patched as of `2.8.11`, which escapes the saved csv with single quotes. As a workaround, avoid opening csv files generated by `gradio` with Excel or similar spreadsheet programs.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) due to insufficient CORS validation in the file upload functionality implemented in gradio/routes.py. The vulnerability allows malicious third-party websites to make unauthorized requests to locally running Gradio applications without proper origin validation, enabling attackers to bypass intended security restrictions.

A path traversal vulnerability exists in the Gradio Audio component of gradio-app/gradio, as of version git 98cbcae. This vulnerability allows an attacker to control the format of the audio file, leading to arbitrary file content deletion. By manipulating the output format, an attacker can reset any file to an empty file, causing a denial of service (DOS) on the server.

A vulnerability in the dataframe component of gradio-app/gradio (version git 98cbcae) allows for a zip bomb attack. The component uses pd.read_csv to process input values, which can accept compressed files. An attacker can exploit this by uploading a maliciously crafted zip bomb, leading to a server crash and causing a denial of service.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to mocked OAuth routes storing the host machine’s Hugging Face access token in a client-side session cookie and using a hardcoded session signing secret. The issue occurs in gradio/oauth.py within attach_oauth(), _add_mocked_oauth_routes(), and _get_mocked_oauth_info(), where visiting /login/huggingface leads to /login/callback and sets request.session["oauth_info"] (including access_token from huggingface_hub.get_token()), while Starlette SessionMiddleware derives the secret from an unset OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET as a constant "-v4" value and stores session data as base64-encoded plaintext in the cookie.

A Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability exists in the gradio-app/gradio repository, affecting the gr.Datetime component. The affected version is git commit 98cbcae. The vulnerability arises from the use of a regular expression ^(?:\s*now\s*(?:-\s*(\d+)\s*([dmhs]))?)?\s*$ to process user input. In Python's default regex engine, this regular expression can take polynomial time to match certain crafted inputs. An attacker can exploit this by sending a crafted HTTP request, causing the gradio process to consume 100% CPU and potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition on the server.

Affected versions of the gradio package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to improper validation of file paths in the File and UploadButton components. The vulnerability exists in the `client_utils.is_file_obj_with_meta` function, which only validates file paths when specific metadata fields are present, specifically requiring both a `meta` key and `_type` value of `gradio.FileData` to trigger path sanitization, allowing attackers to bypass validation by omitting these fields from requests. An attacker with access to a Gradio application that uses File or UploadButton components to preview file content can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted API requests without the required metadata fields, enabling them to read arbitrary files from the application server, including sensitive system files like /etc/passwd.

A vulnerability classified as problematic has been found in gradio-app gradio up to 5.29.1. This affects the function is_valid_origin of the component CORS Handler. The manipulation of the argument localhost_aliases leads to erweiterte Rechte. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The complexity of an attack is rather high. The exploitability is said to be difficult. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure, but did not respond in any way.

Affected versions of the Gradio package are vulnerable to Access Control Bypass due to insufficient case normalization in file path validation logic. The vulnerability exists because the Access Control List (ACL) does not account for variations in letter case when validating file or directory paths. An attacker can exploit this on case-insensitive file systems, such as Windows and macOS, by altering the letter case of a blocked path to gain unauthorized access to sensitive files, potentially leading to information disclosure.

gramps-webapi.advisory: Affected versions of the gramps-webapi package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to insufficient sanitization of private sub-object data in list API endpoints. The ModifiedPrivateProxyDb class inherits the behaviour of PrivateProxyDb.iter_*() methods from Gramps core, which correctly filter out top-level private objects but return remaining objects without stripping private sub-object references such as alternate names, addresses, and note or citation handles. A user with the Guest role can query list endpoints such as GET /api/people/ or GET /api/places/ to obtain private sub-object data attached to otherwise-public objects, resulting in unauthorised exposure of sensitive information.

Affected versions of the gramps-webapi package are vulnerable to Path Traversal (Zip Slip) due to insufficient validation of ZIP entry names during media archive import. The MediaImporter._check_disk_space_and_extract() method in gramps_webapi/api/media_importer.py calls zipfile.extractall() without sanitising entry names containing "dot-dot-slash" sequences, allowing files to be written outside the intended temporary extraction directory. An authenticated attacker with owner-level privileges can upload a crafted ZIP archive to write arbitrary files to the server filesystem, potentially overwriting database files, media files, or configuration files in multi-tree deployments.
